overview.main_flow_diagram:
flowchart TD
    START([Program Start]):::start

    INIT[1: Program Initialization
Retrieve trigger data from CICS
Set queue name and wait interval]:::process
    MQTM[(CICS Trigger Data)]:::datasource

    OPEN_Q[2: Request Queue Open
Open MQ request queue
in shared input mode]:::process
    REQ_MQ[(Request MQ Queue)]:::datasource

    OPEN_OK{Queue Opened
Successfully?}:::decision

    READ_MSG[3: Authorization Request Message Read
Read next message from MQ queue
Capture correlation ID and reply-to queue]:::process
    REQ_MQ2[(Request MQ Queue)]:::datasource

    MSG_AVAIL{Message
Available?}:::decision

    LIMIT_CHECK{Processing Limit
500 messages
reached?}:::decision

    EXTRACT[4: Authorization Request Message Parse
Extract card number, transaction amount,
merchant details, transaction ID,
auth date/time, processing codes]:::process

    AMT_CONV[5: Transaction Amount Conversion
Convert transaction amount from
alphanumeric string to numeric value]:::process

    SCHED_PSB[20: IMS PSB Scheduling
Schedule IMS PSB for database access
Terminate and reschedule if already active]:::process

    READ_XREF[6: Card Cross-Reference Lookup
Look up card number to retrieve
associated account ID and customer ID]:::process
    CCXREF[(CCXREF: Card Cross-Reference
CICS VSAM File)]:::datasource

    CARD_FOUND{Card Found
in Cross-Reference?}:::decision

    READ_ACCT[7: Account Record Retrieval
Read account master record
Retrieve credit limit, balance,
and account status]:::process
    ACCTDAT[(ACCTDAT: Account Master
CICS VSAM File)]:::datasource

    READ_CUST[8: Customer Record Retrieval
Read customer master record
Retrieve customer profile information]:::process
    CUSTDAT[(CUSTDAT: Customer Master
CICS VSAM File)]:::datasource

    READ_SUMRY[9: Pending Authorization Summary Retrieval
Query IMS for existing pending
authorization summary for the account]:::process
    PAUTSUM0[(PAUTSUM0: Pending Auth Summary
IMS Root Segment)]:::datasource

    AVAIL_CREDIT[10: Available Credit Calculation
Calculate available credit:
Credit Limit minus Current Balance
Using IMS summary or account master data]:::process

    DECISION[11: Authorization Decision
Compare transaction amount
against available credit
Approve or Decline]:::process

    DECLINE_DEC{Authorization
Declined?}:::decision

    DECLINE_REASON[12: Decline Reason Assignment
Assign decline reason code:
3100=Card Not Found
4100=Insufficient Funds
4200=Card Not Active
4300=Account Closed
5100=Card Fraud
5200=Merchant Fraud]:::process

    BUILD_RESP[13: Authorization Response Preparation
Build response message:
Card number, Transaction ID,
Auth ID code, Response code
00=Approved / 05=Declined
Decline reason, Approved amount]:::process

    SEND_RESP[14: Authorization Response Send
Send authorization decision
back to requester via MQ reply queue
using saved correlation ID]:::process
    REPLY_MQ[(Reply MQ Queue)]:::datasource

    CARD_FOUND_DB{Card Found
in Cross-Reference?}:::decision

    UPDATE_SUMRY[15: Authorization Summary Update
Update pending authorization summary in IMS:
Approved: increment count and balance
Declined: increment declined count
Create new record if not exists]:::process
    PAUTSUM0B[(PAUTSUM0: Pending Auth Summary
IMS Root Segment)]:::datasource

    INSERT_DTL[16: Authorization Detail Record Insert
Insert new authorization detail record
in IMS as child segment under summary
Capture all transaction and merchant details
Status: Pending or Declined]:::process
    PAUTDTL1[(PAUTDTL1: Auth Detail
IMS Child Segment)]:::datasource

    TIMESTAMP[17: Authorization Timestamp Generation
Generate timestamp with millisecond precision
Compute reverse chronological sort key
for date and time fields]:::process

    COMMIT[19: Transaction Commit
Issue syncpoint to commit
all database updates]:::process

    LOOP_CTRL[18: Message Processing Loop Control
Process next message or
check loop termination conditions]:::process

    TERMINATE[21: Program Termination
Terminate IMS PSB session
Close MQ request queue]:::process

    CLOSE_Q[22: Request Queue Close
Close MQ request queue connection]:::process

    LOG_ERROR[23: Error Logging
Log error/warning with timestamp,
program name, transaction ID,
error location, codes, and message]:::process
    ERR_Q[(CSSL: Error Log Queue)]:::datasource

    CRITICAL_ERR{Critical
Error?}:::decision

    CRIT_HANDLE[24: Critical Error Handling
Terminate IMS PSB and
close MQ connections
before ending program]:::process

    PROG_END([Program End]):::final

    %% Main Flow
    START --> INIT
    MQTM -.->|Retrieve Trigger Data| INIT
    INIT --> OPEN_Q
    REQ_MQ -.->|Open Queue| OPEN_Q
    OPEN_Q --> OPEN_OK

    OPEN_OK -->|No - Queue Open Failed| LOG_ERROR
    OPEN_OK -->|Yes| READ_MSG
    REQ_MQ2 -.->|Read Message| READ_MSG

    READ_MSG --> MSG_AVAIL
    MSG_AVAIL -->|No Messages Available| TERMINATE

    MSG_AVAIL -->|Message Available| EXTRACT
    EXTRACT --> AMT_CONV
    AMT_CONV --> SCHED_PSB
    SCHED_PSB --> READ_XREF
    CCXREF -.->|Lookup Card Number| READ_XREF

    READ_XREF --> CARD_FOUND
    CARD_FOUND -->|Card Not Found| DECISION
    CARD_FOUND -->|Card Found| READ_ACCT
    ACCTDAT -.->|Read Account Record| READ_ACCT
    READ_ACCT --> READ_CUST
    CUSTDAT -.->|Read Customer Record| READ_CUST
    READ_CUST --> READ_SUMRY
    PAUTSUM0 -.->|Query Pending Auth Summary| READ_SUMRY
    READ_SUMRY --> AVAIL_CREDIT
    AVAIL_CREDIT --> DECISION

    DECISION --> DECLINE_DEC
    DECLINE_DEC -->|Yes - Declined| DECLINE_REASON
    DECLINE_REASON --> BUILD_RESP
    DECLINE_DEC -->|No - Approved| BUILD_RESP

    BUILD_RESP --> SEND_RESP
    REPLY_MQ -.->|Send Response| SEND_RESP

    SEND_RESP --> CARD_FOUND_DB
    CARD_FOUND_DB -->|Card Not Found - Skip DB Write| COMMIT
    CARD_FOUND_DB -->|Card Found - Write to DB| TIMESTAMP
    TIMESTAMP --> UPDATE_SUMRY
    PAUTSUM0B -.->|Update/Insert Summary Record| UPDATE_SUMRY
    UPDATE_SUMRY --> INSERT_DTL
    PAUTDTL1 -.->|Insert Detail Record| INSERT_DTL
    INSERT_DTL --> COMMIT

    COMMIT --> LOOP_CTRL
    LOOP_CTRL --> LIMIT_CHECK
    LIMIT_CHECK -->|Limit Reached| TERMINATE
    LIMIT_CHECK -->|Continue Processing| READ_MSG

    %% Termination
    TERMINATE --> CLOSE_Q
    CLOSE_Q --> PROG_END

    %% Error Logging Flow
    LOG_ERROR --> ERR_Q
    ERR_Q -.->|Write Error Log| LOG_ERROR
    LOG_ERROR --> CRITICAL_ERR
    CRITICAL_ERR -->|Yes| CRIT_HANDLE
    CRITICAL_ERR -->|No - Warning Only| PROG_END
    CRIT_HANDLE --> TERMINATE

rules.rule_name: Program Initialization via CICS Trigger Data Retrieval
rules.rule_description: When the program is triggered by a CICS trigger monitor, it retrieves the trigger message to identify the MQ request queue name and trigger data, and sets the message wait interval for subsequent queue reads.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
1: Program Initialization
Retrieve trigger data from CICS
Set queue name and wait interval

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program is started by a CICS trigger monitor with a trigger message containing the MQ queue name and trigger data
acceptance_criteria.When: The program initializes and retrieves the trigger message from CICS
acceptance_criteria.Then: The MQ request queue name is set from the trigger message queue name field, the trigger data is captured from the trigger message trigger data field, and the message wait interval is set to 5000 milliseconds for all subsequent queue read operations

rules.rule_name: MQ Request Queue Open in Shared Input Mode
rules.rule_description: The program opens the MQ request queue in shared input mode using the queue name retrieved from the trigger data, allowing multiple consumers to read from the same queue concurrently.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
2: Request Queue Open
Open MQ request queue
in shared input mode

acceptance_criteria.Given: The MQ request queue name has been retrieved from the CICS trigger data
acceptance_criteria.When: The program attempts to open the MQ request queue
acceptance_criteria.Then: The queue is opened in shared input mode; if the queue opens successfully, the queue is marked as open and processing continues; if the queue fails to open, a critical MQ error is logged with error location 'M001', error codes capturing the completion code and reason code, and the message 'REQ MQ OPEN ERROR', and the program terminates immediately

rules.rule_name: Authorization Request Message Read from MQ Queue
rules.rule_description: The program reads the next available authorization request message from the MQ request queue, capturing the correlation ID and reply-to queue name needed to route the response back to the requester.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
3: Authorization Request Message Read
Read next message from MQ queue
Capture correlation ID and reply-to queue

acceptance_criteria.Given: The MQ request queue is open and the program is ready to process authorization requests
acceptance_criteria.When: The program attempts to read the next message from the MQ request queue with a wait interval of 5000 milliseconds
acceptance_criteria.Then: If a message is successfully retrieved, the message correlation ID is saved and the reply-to queue name is captured for later response routing; if no message is available, the no-more-messages flag is set and the processing loop ends; if a read error occurs, a critical error is logged with error location 'M003', completion code, reason code, and the message 'FAILED TO READ REQUEST MQ' along with the card number as the event key, and the program terminates immediately

rules.rule_name: Authorization Request Message Parsing
rules.rule_description: Each authorization request message is a comma-delimited string that must be parsed into its individual data fields covering card details, transaction information, and merchant information.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
4: Authorization Request Message Parse
Extract card number, transaction amount,
merchant details, transaction ID,
auth date/time, processing codes

acceptance_criteria.Given: A raw authorization request message has been successfully read from the MQ request queue
acceptance_criteria.When: The program parses the comma-delimited message content
acceptance_criteria.Then: The following 18 fields are extracted in order: Authorization Date, Authorization Time, Card Number, Authorization Type, Card Expiry Date, Message Type, Message Source, Processing Code, Transaction Amount (as alphanumeric string), Merchant Category Code, Acquirer Country Code, POS Entry Mode, Merchant ID, Merchant Name, Merchant City, Merchant State, Merchant ZIP, and Transaction ID

rules.rule_name: Transaction Amount Conversion from Alphanumeric to Numeric
rules.rule_description: The transaction amount arrives in the request message as an alphanumeric string and must be converted to a numeric value before it can be used in credit availability calculations.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
5: Transaction Amount Conversion
Convert transaction amount from
alphanumeric string to numeric value

acceptance_criteria.Given: The transaction amount has been extracted from the request message as an alphanumeric string
acceptance_criteria.When: The program converts the transaction amount for use in authorization processing
acceptance_criteria.Then: The alphanumeric transaction amount string is converted to a numeric value using the NUMVAL function, and the resulting numeric transaction amount is stored for use in credit availability and authorization decision calculations

rules.rule_name: IMS PSB Scheduling for Database Access
rules.rule_description: Before accessing IMS database segments for pending authorization summary and detail records, the program must schedule the IMS Program Specification Block (PSB). If the PSB is already active from a prior cycle, it is terminated and rescheduled.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
20: IMS PSB Scheduling
Schedule IMS PSB for database access
Terminate and reschedule if already active

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program needs to access IMS database segments for authorization processing
acceptance_criteria.When: The program schedules the IMS PSB
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the PSB is not already scheduled, it is scheduled normally; if the PSB was already scheduled from a previous iteration, it is first terminated and then rescheduled; if scheduling succeeds, the IMS PSB scheduled flag is set to true; if scheduling fails, a critical IMS error is logged with error location 'I001', the IMS return code, and the message 'IMS SCHD FAILED', and the program terminates immediately

rules.rule_name: Card Number Validation via Cross-Reference Lookup
rules.rule_description: Every authorization request must be validated by looking up the card number in the Card Cross-Reference file to retrieve the associated account ID and customer ID required for further processing.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
6: Card Cross-Reference Lookup
Look up card number to retrieve
associated account ID and customer ID

acceptance_criteria.Given: A card number has been extracted from the authorization request message
acceptance_criteria.When: The program looks up the card number in the Card Cross-Reference (CCXREF) VSAM file
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the card is found, the associated account ID and customer ID are retrieved and the card-found flag is set to true; if the card is not found, the card-not-found flag is set, the account-not-found flag is set, a warning is logged with error location 'A001', the message 'CARD NOT FOUND IN XREF', and the card number as the event key, and processing continues directly to the authorization decision without reading account or customer records; if a file access error occurs, a critical error is logged with error location 'C001', the response code, reason code, and the message 'FAILED TO READ XREF FILE' with the card number as the event key, and the program terminates immediately

rules.rule_name: Account Master Record Retrieval
rules.rule_description: When a card is found in the cross-reference, the associated account master record is retrieved using the account ID from the cross-reference to obtain the credit limit, current balance, and account status needed for authorization decisions.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
7: Account Record Retrieval
Read account master record
Retrieve credit limit, balance,
and account status

acceptance_criteria.Given: The card number has been found in the Card Cross-Reference file and an account ID has been retrieved
acceptance_criteria.When: The program reads the account master record from the Account Master (ACCTDAT) VSAM file using the account ID
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the account record is found, the account-found flag is set to true and the credit limit, current balance, and account details are available for authorization processing; if the account is not found, the account-not-found flag is set, a warning is logged with error location 'A002', the message 'ACCT NOT FOUND IN XREF', and the account ID as the event key; if a file access error occurs, a critical error is logged with error location 'C002', the response code, reason code, and the message 'FAILED TO READ ACCT FILE' with the account ID as the event key, and the program terminates immediately

rules.rule_name: Customer Master Record Retrieval
rules.rule_description: When a card is found in the cross-reference, the associated customer master record is retrieved using the customer ID from the cross-reference to obtain the customer profile information.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
8: Customer Record Retrieval
Read customer master record
Retrieve customer profile information

acceptance_criteria.Given: The card number has been found in the Card Cross-Reference file and a customer ID has been retrieved
acceptance_criteria.When: The program reads the customer master record from the Customer Master (CUSTDAT) VSAM file using the customer ID
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the customer record is found, the customer-found flag is set to true and customer profile information is available; if the customer is not found, the customer-not-found flag is set, a warning is logged with error location 'A003', the message 'CUST NOT FOUND IN XREF', and the customer ID as the event key; if a file access error occurs, a critical error is logged with error location 'C003', the response code, reason code, and the message 'FAILED TO READ CUST FILE' with the customer ID as the event key, and the program terminates immediately

rules.rule_name: Pending Authorization Summary Retrieval from IMS
rules.rule_description: The program queries the IMS database for an existing pending authorization summary record for the account to obtain the most current credit limit and credit balance reflecting all previously approved but not yet settled authorizations.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
9: Pending Authorization Summary Retrieval
Query IMS for existing pending
authorization summary for the account

acceptance_criteria.Given: The account ID has been retrieved from the Card Cross-Reference file
acceptance_criteria.When: The program queries the IMS PAUTSUM0 segment for a pending authorization summary record matching the account ID
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the summary record is found, the pending-auth-summary-found flag is set to true and the credit limit and credit balance from the summary are available for available credit calculation; if no summary record exists for the account, the pending-auth-summary-not-found flag is set and the program will fall back to using the account master record for credit calculation; if an IMS access error occurs, a critical error is logged with error location 'I002', the IMS return code, and the message 'IMS GET SUMMARY FAILED' with the card number as the event key, and the program terminates immediately

rules.rule_name: Available Credit Calculation Using Pending Authorization Summary
rules.rule_description: When a pending authorization summary record exists for the account, the available credit is calculated using the credit limit and credit balance from the IMS pending authorization summary, which reflects the most current state including all previously approved but unsettled authorizations.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
10: Available Credit Calculation
Calculate available credit:
Credit Limit minus Current Balance
Using IMS summary or account master data

acceptance_criteria.Given: A pending authorization summary record has been found in IMS for the account
acceptance_criteria.When: The program calculates the available credit for the authorization decision
acceptance_criteria.Then: The available credit amount is calculated as: Available Amount = Credit Limit (from Pending Auth Summary) minus Credit Balance (from Pending Auth Summary)

rules.rule_name: Available Credit Calculation Using Account Master as Fallback
rules.rule_description: When no pending authorization summary record exists for the account in IMS, the available credit is calculated using the credit limit and current balance from the account master record as a fallback.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
10: Available Credit Calculation
Calculate available credit:
Credit Limit minus Current Balance
Using IMS summary or account master data

acceptance_criteria.Given: No pending authorization summary record exists in IMS for the account, but the account master record has been found
acceptance_criteria.When: The program calculates the available credit for the authorization decision
acceptance_criteria.Then: The available credit amount is calculated as: Available Amount = Account Credit Limit (from Account Master) minus Account Current Balance (from Account Master)

rules.rule_name: Authorization Approval Decision Based on Available Credit
rules.rule_description: The core authorization decision compares the requested transaction amount against the calculated available credit to determine whether to approve or decline the transaction.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
11: Authorization Decision
Compare transaction amount
against available credit
Approve or Decline

acceptance_criteria.Given: The transaction amount and available credit amount have been determined
acceptance_criteria.When: The program compares the transaction amount against the available credit
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the transaction amount is less than or equal to the available credit, the authorization is approved with response code '00' and the approved amount is set equal to the transaction amount; if the transaction amount exceeds the available credit, the authorization is declined with the insufficient-funds flag set, response code '05', approved amount set to zero, and decline reason code '4100'

rules.rule_name: Authorization Decline When No Account Data Exists
rules.rule_description: When neither a pending authorization summary nor an account master record can be found for the card, the transaction is unconditionally declined as there is no basis for credit evaluation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
11: Authorization Decision
Compare transaction amount
against available credit
Approve or Decline

acceptance_criteria.Given: The card was found in the cross-reference but neither a pending authorization summary nor an account master record exists for the account
acceptance_criteria.When: The program evaluates the authorization decision
acceptance_criteria.Then: The authorization is unconditionally declined with response code '05' and approved amount set to zero, as there is insufficient account data to evaluate the credit availability

rules.rule_name: Authorization Decline When Card Not Found in Cross-Reference
rules.rule_description: When the card number is not found in the Card Cross-Reference file, the transaction is declined without any credit evaluation, as the card cannot be associated with a valid account.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
11: Authorization Decision
Compare transaction amount
against available credit
Approve or Decline

acceptance_criteria.Given: The card number from the authorization request was not found in the Card Cross-Reference file
acceptance_criteria.When: The program reaches the authorization decision step
acceptance_criteria.Then: The authorization is declined with response code '05', approved amount set to zero, and decline reason code '3100' assigned to indicate the card, account, or customer was not found

rules.rule_name: Decline Reason Code Assignment
rules.rule_description: When an authorization is declined, a specific reason code is assigned to explain the cause of the decline, enabling the requester to understand and communicate the reason to the cardholder.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
12: Decline Reason Assignment
Assign decline reason code:
3100=Card Not Found
4100=Insufficient Funds
4200=Card Not Active
4300=Account Closed
5100=Card Fraud
5200=Merchant Fraud

acceptance_criteria.Given: An authorization has been declined
acceptance_criteria.When: The program assigns the decline reason code
acceptance_criteria.Then: The reason code is assigned based on the following priority: '3100' if the card was not found in the cross-reference, or the account was not found, or the customer was not found; '4100' if the decline was due to insufficient available credit; '4200' if the card is not active; '4300' if the account is closed; '5100' if the card is flagged for fraud; '5200' if the merchant is flagged for fraud; '9000' for any other unspecified decline reason; if the authorization is approved, the reason code is set to '0000'

rules.rule_name: Authorization Response Message Construction
rules.rule_description: After the authorization decision is made, a comma-delimited response message is constructed containing all fields required by the requester to process the authorization outcome.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
13: Authorization Response Preparation
Build response message:
Card number, Transaction ID,
Auth ID code, Response code
00=Approved / 05=Declined
Decline reason, Approved amount

acceptance_criteria.Given: The authorization decision has been made with all response fields populated
acceptance_criteria.When: The program builds the authorization response message
acceptance_criteria.Then: A comma-delimited response message is constructed containing the following six fields in order: Card Number, Transaction ID, Authorization ID Code (set from the authorization time), Response Code ('00' for approved or '05' for declined), Authorization Response Reason Code ('0000' for approved or the specific decline reason code), and Approved Amount (equal to the transaction amount for approvals or zero for declines)

rules.rule_name: Authorization Response Delivery via MQ Reply Queue
rules.rule_description: The authorization response message is sent back to the requester through the MQ reply queue specified in the original request, correlated to the original request message to enable the requester to match the response.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
14: Authorization Response Send
Send authorization decision
back to requester via MQ reply queue
using saved correlation ID

acceptance_criteria.Given: The authorization response message has been built and the reply-to queue name and correlation ID were captured from the original request message
acceptance_criteria.When: The program sends the authorization response
acceptance_criteria.Then: The response message is sent to the reply-to queue specified in the original request using the saved correlation ID to correlate the response to the original request; the message is sent as non-persistent with an expiry of 50 units and message type set to reply; if the send fails, a critical error is logged with error location 'M004', the completion code, reason code, and the message 'FAILED TO PUT ON REPLY MQ' with the card number as the event key, and the program terminates immediately

rules.rule_name: Authorization Summary Update for Approved Transactions
rules.rule_description: When an authorization is approved, the pending authorization summary record in IMS is updated to reflect the new approved authorization, incrementing counts, updating the approved amount total, and increasing the credit balance.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
15: Authorization Summary Update
Update pending authorization summary in IMS:
Approved: increment count and balance
Declined: increment declined count
Create new record if not exists

acceptance_criteria.Given: The authorization has been approved and the card was found in the cross-reference
acceptance_criteria.When: The program updates the pending authorization summary in IMS
acceptance_criteria.Then: The credit limit and cash credit limit are refreshed from the account master record; the approved authorization count is incremented by 1; the approved authorization amount total is increased by the approved amount; the credit balance is increased by the approved amount; the cash balance is set to zero; if a summary record already existed it is replaced, if no summary record existed a new one is inserted with the account ID and customer ID from the cross-reference; if the IMS update or insert fails, a critical error is logged with error location 'I003', the IMS return code, and the message 'IMS UPDATE SUMRY FAILED' with the card number as the event key, and the program terminates immediately

rules.rule_name: Authorization Summary Update for Declined Transactions
rules.rule_description: When an authorization is declined, the pending authorization summary record in IMS is updated to track the declined authorization count and total declined amount for reporting and monitoring purposes.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
15: Authorization Summary Update
Update pending authorization summary in IMS:
Approved: increment count and balance
Declined: increment declined count
Create new record if not exists

acceptance_criteria.Given: The authorization has been declined and the card was found in the cross-reference
acceptance_criteria.When: The program updates the pending authorization summary in IMS
acceptance_criteria.Then: The credit limit and cash credit limit are refreshed from the account master record; the declined authorization count is incremented by 1; the declined authorization amount total is increased by the transaction amount; if a summary record already existed it is replaced, if no summary record existed a new one is inserted with the account ID and customer ID from the cross-reference; if the IMS update or insert fails, a critical error is logged with error location 'I003', the IMS return code, and the message 'IMS UPDATE SUMRY FAILED' with the card number as the event key, and the program terminates immediately

rules.rule_name: Authorization Detail Record Insertion into IMS
rules.rule_description: A complete authorization detail record is inserted into IMS as a child segment under the account's authorization summary, capturing all transaction, merchant, and response details for audit and settlement purposes.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
16: Authorization Detail Record Insert
Insert new authorization detail record
in IMS as child segment under summary
Capture all transaction and merchant details
Status: Pending or Declined

acceptance_criteria.Given: The authorization summary has been updated and the card was found in the cross-reference
acceptance_criteria.When: The program inserts the authorization detail record into IMS under the account's summary segment (PAUTDTL1 as child of PAUTSUM0)
acceptance_criteria.Then: A new detail record is inserted containing: Authorization Date and Time, Card Number, Authorization Type, Card Expiry Date, Message Type, Message Source, Processing Code, Transaction Amount, Merchant Category Code, Acquirer Country Code, POS Entry Mode, Merchant ID, Merchant Name, Merchant City, Merchant State, Merchant ZIP, Transaction ID, Authorization ID Code, Response Code, Response Reason Code, and Approved Amount; the authorization status is set to 'PENDING MATCH' for approved transactions or 'AUTH DECLINED' for declined transactions; the fraud flag and fraud report date are initialized to blank; if the IMS insert fails, a critical error is logged with error location 'I004', the IMS return code, and the message 'IMS INSERT DETL FAILED' with the card number as the event key, and the program terminates immediately

rules.rule_name: Authorization Timestamp Generation with Reverse Chronological Sort Key
rules.rule_description: Before inserting the authorization detail record, a precise timestamp is generated and complement values are computed for the date and time fields to enable reverse chronological retrieval of authorization history.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
17: Authorization Timestamp Generation
Generate timestamp with millisecond precision
Compute reverse chronological sort key
for date and time fields

acceptance_criteria.Given: The authorization decision has been made and the program is preparing to write the detail record to IMS
acceptance_criteria.When: The program generates the authorization timestamp
acceptance_criteria.Then: The current date is captured in YYDDD format and the current time is captured with millisecond precision; a reverse chronological sort key for the date is computed as 99999 minus the current YYDDD date; a reverse chronological sort key for the time is computed as 999999999 minus the current time including milliseconds; these complement values are stored in the authorization detail record so that the most recent authorization appears first when records are retrieved in ascending key order

rules.rule_name: Transaction Commit After Each Authorization
rules.rule_description: After each authorization request is fully processed — including the decision, response sent, and all database updates — a commit point is issued to permanently save all changes, ensuring each authorization is independently committed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
19: Transaction Commit
Issue syncpoint to commit
all database updates

acceptance_criteria.Given: An authorization request has been fully processed with the decision made, response sent to the requester, and all IMS database updates completed
acceptance_criteria.When: The program issues a syncpoint
acceptance_criteria.Then: All database updates for the current authorization (summary update and detail insert) are permanently committed; the IMS PSB scheduled flag is reset to not-scheduled so that a fresh PSB will be obtained for the next authorization message

rules.rule_name: Message Processing Loop Control and Limit Enforcement
rules.rule_description: After each authorization is committed, the program checks whether the processing limit has been reached to decide whether to continue processing more messages or terminate the current execution cycle.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
18: Message Processing Loop Control
Process next message or
check loop termination conditions

acceptance_criteria.Given: An authorization message has been fully processed and committed
acceptance_criteria.When: The program evaluates whether to continue processing
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the number of messages processed exceeds the configured processing limit, the loop-end flag is set and the program proceeds to termination; if the processing limit has not been reached, the program reads the next message from the MQ request queue and continues the processing loop

rules.rule_name: Program Termination and Resource Cleanup
rules.rule_description: When all messages have been processed or the processing limit is reached, the program performs an orderly termination by releasing all acquired resources.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
21: Program Termination
Terminate IMS PSB session
Close MQ request queue

acceptance_criteria.Given: The message processing loop has ended either because no more messages are available or the processing limit has been reached
acceptance_criteria.When: The program executes the termination sequence
acceptance_criteria.Then: If an IMS PSB session is currently active, it is terminated; the MQ request queue close procedure is invoked to release the queue connection

rules.rule_name: MQ Request Queue Close
rules.rule_description: As part of program termination, the MQ request queue connection is closed to release the queue resource.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
22: Request Queue Close
Close MQ request queue connection

acceptance_criteria.Given: The MQ request queue was successfully opened earlier in the program
acceptance_criteria.When: The program closes the MQ request queue during termination
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the queue was opened, the MQCLOSE call is made to close the queue connection; if the close is successful, the queue is marked as closed; if the close fails, a warning (non-critical) error is logged with error location 'M005', the completion code, reason code, and the message 'FAILED TO CLOSE REQUEST MQ', and processing continues to program end

rules.rule_name: Error Logging with Severity Classification
rules.rule_description: All errors and warnings encountered during processing are logged to the error log queue with full context information including timestamp, program identification, error location, error codes, and a descriptive message.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
23: Error Logging
Log error/warning with timestamp,
program name, transaction ID,
error location, codes, and message

acceptance_criteria.Given: An error or warning condition has been detected during authorization processing
acceptance_criteria.When: The program logs the error
acceptance_criteria.Then: The current timestamp (date and time) is captured; the error log record is written to the CSSL transient data queue containing: the CICS transaction ID as the application identifier, the program name, the current date, the current time, the error location code, error codes, and the error message; if the error is classified as critical, the program immediately invokes the critical error handler to terminate; if the error is classified as a warning, processing continues after logging

rules.rule_name: Critical Error Handling and Forced Program Termination
rules.rule_description: When a critical error is encountered, the program performs an orderly shutdown by releasing all resources before terminating, ensuring no resources are left in an inconsistent state.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
24: Critical Error Handling
Terminate IMS PSB and
close MQ connections
before ending program

acceptance_criteria.Given: A critical error has been logged that prevents the program from continuing normal processing
acceptance_criteria.When: The program executes the critical error handler
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program invokes the termination sequence to release all resources: if an IMS PSB session is active it is terminated, and if the MQ request queue is open it is closed; after resource cleanup the program ends immediately without processing any further authorization messages

rules.rule_name: Retrieve Trigger Data from CICS at Program Startup
rules.rule_description: At program initialization, the system retrieves trigger data from CICS to identify the incoming authorization request queue and associated processing parameters.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Retrieve Trigger Data from CICS

acceptance_criteria.Given: The authorization processing program has been started by a CICS trigger event
acceptance_criteria.When: The program begins initialization and requests trigger data from CICS
acceptance_criteria.Then: The trigger data containing the request queue name and trigger processing details is retrieved and made available for subsequent initialization steps

rules.rule_name: Validate Successful Retrieval of Trigger Data
rules.rule_description: The program checks whether the CICS trigger data was successfully retrieved before attempting to extract queue name and trigger details. If retrieval was not successful, the program proceeds with default settings without setting queue name or trigger data from the trigger message.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Trigger Data Retrieved Successfully?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program has attempted to retrieve trigger data from CICS during initialization
acceptance_criteria.When: The CICS response is evaluated to determine if the retrieval completed normally
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the CICS response indicates a normal successful retrieval, the program proceeds to extract the request queue name and trigger data from the trigger message; if the response indicates any other condition (non-normal), the program bypasses queue name and trigger data extraction and proceeds directly to set the message wait interval using default settings

rules.rule_name: Set Request Queue Name from Trigger Message
rules.rule_description: When trigger data is successfully retrieved, the authorization request queue name is extracted from the trigger message and stored for use in opening and reading the incoming authorization request queue.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Request Queue Name from Trigger Data

acceptance_criteria.Given: The CICS trigger data has been successfully retrieved and contains a valid queue name
acceptance_criteria.When: The program extracts the queue name from the trigger message data
acceptance_criteria.Then: The request queue name is set from the queue name field (QNAME) of the trigger message, and this queue name will be used to open the authorization request queue in the next processing step

rules.rule_name: Set Trigger Data for Authorization Processing
rules.rule_description: When trigger data is successfully retrieved, the trigger data field from the trigger message is captured and stored for use during the authorization processing cycle.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Trigger Data for Processing

acceptance_criteria.Given: The CICS trigger data has been successfully retrieved and contains trigger processing information
acceptance_criteria.When: The program extracts the trigger data field from the trigger message
acceptance_criteria.Then: The trigger data is set from the trigger data field (TRIGGERDATA) of the trigger message and stored for use during the authorization processing session

rules.rule_name: Apply Default Processing Settings When Trigger Data Unavailable
rules.rule_description: When trigger data cannot be successfully retrieved from CICS, the program does not set the request queue name or trigger data from the trigger message, and instead proceeds with whatever default queue name and processing parameters are already configured in the program.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: No - Use Default Settings

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program has attempted to retrieve trigger data from CICS during initialization
acceptance_criteria.When: The CICS response indicates the trigger data retrieval was not successful (non-normal response)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program does not update the request queue name or trigger data fields from the trigger message, and proceeds directly to set the message wait interval using the pre-configured default values already present in the program's working storage

rules.rule_name: Set Message Wait Interval for Queue Reading
rules.rule_description: Regardless of whether trigger data was successfully retrieved or not, the program always sets the message wait interval to 5000 milliseconds. This interval controls how long the program will wait for an authorization request message to arrive in the queue before determining that no messages are available.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Message Wait Interval to 5000 milliseconds

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program is completing its initialization phase, either after successfully extracting trigger data or after defaulting due to unsuccessful trigger data retrieval
acceptance_criteria.When: The program sets the wait interval parameter for message queue reading operations
acceptance_criteria.Then: The message wait interval is unconditionally set to 5000 milliseconds, meaning the program will wait up to 5 seconds for each authorization request message to arrive in the request queue before concluding no messages are available

rules.rule_name: Set Request Queue Name from Initialization Parameters
rules.rule_description: Before opening the authorization request queue, the system must configure the target queue identity using the queue name retrieved during program initialization from the MQ trigger message.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Target Queue Name from Initialization Parameters

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program has been initialized and the authorization request queue name has been retrieved from the MQ trigger message and stored as the request queue name parameter
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares to open the authorization request queue
acceptance_criteria.Then: The target queue descriptor must be populated with the queue name from the initialization parameters, identifying the correct queue from which authorization request messages will be read

rules.rule_name: Open Authorization Request Queue in Shared Input Mode
rules.rule_description: The authorization request queue must be opened in shared input mode, allowing the program to read pending authorization request messages while permitting other consumers to access the same queue concurrently.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Open MQ Request Queue in Shared Input Mode

acceptance_criteria.Given: The request queue name has been set from initialization parameters and the queue descriptor has been configured with the correct queue name and queue type
acceptance_criteria.When: The system attempts to open the authorization request queue using shared input access mode
acceptance_criteria.Then: The queue open operation must be executed with shared input mode options, establishing a connection handle to the request queue that will be used for all subsequent message read operations

rules.rule_name: Mark Request Queue as Open and Ready for Message Reading
rules.rule_description: Upon successfully opening the authorization request queue, the system must record the queue's availability status so that subsequent processing steps know the queue is ready for reading authorization request messages.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Mark Request Queue as Open and Ready for Message Reading

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has attempted to open the authorization request queue in shared input mode
acceptance_criteria.When: The queue open operation completes successfully with no errors
acceptance_criteria.Then: The request queue status must be marked as open and ready, enabling the program to proceed with reading authorization request messages from the queue

rules.rule_name: Log Critical Error and Halt Processing When Request Queue Cannot Be Opened
rules.rule_description: If the authorization request queue cannot be opened, the failure must be recorded as a critical error with full diagnostic details, and all further authorization processing must be immediately halted since no messages can be received.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Log Critical Error: Request Queue Open Failed with Error Codes

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has attempted to open the authorization request queue in shared input mode
acceptance_criteria.When: The queue open operation fails for any reason
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must: (1) record the error location as 'M001', (2) classify the error as a critical MQ error, (3) capture both the completion code and the reason code as error diagnostic details, (4) set the error message to 'REQ MQ OPEN ERROR', (5) write the error log entry, and (6) immediately terminate all authorization processing since no request messages can be received

rules.rule_name: Read Next Authorization Request Message from Queue
rules.rule_description: The system attempts to retrieve the next available authorization request message from the MQ request queue using shared input mode with a configured wait interval, converting the message to the required string format.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Attempt to Read Next Message from MQ Request Queue

acceptance_criteria.Given: The MQ request queue has been successfully opened and is ready to receive messages, and the system is configured with a wait interval of 5000 milliseconds
acceptance_criteria.When: The system attempts to read the next available authorization request message from the MQ request queue
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system retrieves the next message from the queue into the message buffer, capturing the full message data length, and the read operation result (completion code and reason code) is available for further processing

rules.rule_name: Save Correlation ID from Successfully Retrieved Message
rules.rule_description: When an authorization request message is successfully retrieved from the queue, the system saves the message correlation ID from the message header so that the authorization response can be matched back to the original request by the requester.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Save Correlation ID from Message Header for Response Matching

acceptance_criteria.Given: An authorization request message has been successfully read from the MQ request queue (read completion code indicates success)
acceptance_criteria.When: The message is successfully retrieved
acceptance_criteria.Then: The correlation ID from the message descriptor header of the retrieved message is saved into the working storage correlation ID field, to be used later for routing the authorization response back to the original requester

rules.rule_name: Save Reply-To Queue Name from Successfully Retrieved Message
rules.rule_description: When an authorization request message is successfully retrieved from the queue, the system saves the reply-to queue name from the message header so that the authorization response is sent to the correct destination queue specified by the requester.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Save Reply-To Queue Name from Message Header for Response Routing

acceptance_criteria.Given: An authorization request message has been successfully read from the MQ request queue (read completion code indicates success)
acceptance_criteria.When: The message is successfully retrieved
acceptance_criteria.Then: The reply-to queue name from the message descriptor header of the retrieved message is saved into the working storage reply queue name field, to be used later as the destination queue when sending the authorization response

rules.rule_name: Stop Processing Loop When No More Messages Are Available
rules.rule_description: When the system attempts to read from the MQ request queue and the queue contains no more messages, the processing loop is flagged to stop, preventing further attempts to read authorization requests in the current execution cycle.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Flag: No More Messages Available - Stop Processing Loop

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has attempted to read the next authorization request message from the MQ request queue
acceptance_criteria.When: The read attempt fails because no messages are available in the queue (the reason code indicates no message available)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The 'No More Messages Available' flag is set to TRUE, which causes the main authorization processing loop to stop iterating and no further message reads are attempted in the current execution cycle

rules.rule_name: Log Critical Error and Terminate on Unexpected Message Read Failure
rules.rule_description: When the system encounters an unexpected failure while attempting to read an authorization request message from the queue (any failure other than no message available), a critical error is logged with full error details including the card number, and the program is terminated immediately.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Log Critical Error with Error Codes and Card Number

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has attempted to read the next authorization request message from the MQ request queue, and the read has failed
acceptance_criteria.When: The read failure reason is anything other than 'no message available' (i.e., an unexpected or system-level error has occurred)
acceptance_criteria.Then: A critical error log entry is created with: error location code 'M003', error type flagged as critical, error code 1 set to the read completion code, error code 2 set to the read reason code, error message set to 'FAILED TO READ REQUEST MQ', and the card number recorded as the event key; the program then terminates immediately after logging the error

rules.rule_name: Authorization Request Message Format Definition
rules.rule_description: Defines the structure and format of an incoming authorization request message received from the MQ Request Queue. The message is a single text string with all fields separated by commas in a fixed positional sequence of 18 fields.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Receive Raw Message Buffer
Comma-delimited text string
from MQ Request Queue

acceptance_criteria.Given: An authorization request message has arrived in the MQ Request Queue and has been read into the message buffer
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares to parse the authorization request message
acceptance_criteria.Then: The message must be recognized as a comma-delimited text string containing exactly 18 positional fields in the following fixed sequence: Authorization Date, Authorization Time, Card Number, Authorization Type, Card Expiry Date, Message Type, Message Source, Processing Code, Transaction Amount, Merchant Category Code, Acquirer Country Code, POS Entry Mode, Merchant ID, Merchant Name, Merchant City, Merchant State, Merchant ZIP Code, and Transaction ID

rules.rule_name: Parse Authorization Request Message by Comma Delimiter
rules.rule_description: Defines the parsing mechanism for splitting the raw authorization request message into individual data fields using the comma character as the field delimiter, extracting all 18 fields simultaneously in their positional order.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Split Message by Comma Delimiter
Extract All Fields in Sequence

acceptance_criteria.Given: A raw authorization request message buffer has been received from the MQ Request Queue containing all authorization fields as a single comma-delimited text string
acceptance_criteria.When: The system splits the message using the comma character as the delimiter
acceptance_criteria.Then: All 18 fields must be extracted simultaneously in their fixed positional sequence and stored in their respective data fields: Authorization Date, Authorization Time, Card Number, Authorization Type, Card Expiry Date, Message Type, Message Source, Processing Code, Transaction Amount (as text), Merchant Category Code, Acquirer Country Code, POS Entry Mode, Merchant ID, Merchant Name, Merchant City, Merchant State, Merchant ZIP Code, and Transaction ID

rules.rule_name: Extract Transaction Identity Fields from Authorization Request
rules.rule_description: Defines the extraction of the three core transaction identity fields from the first three positional slots of the comma-delimited authorization request message. These fields uniquely identify when and by whom the authorization was initiated.

─────────────────────────
Authorization Date
Authorization Time
Card Number

acceptance_criteria.Given: A comma-delimited authorization request message has been received and is being parsed
acceptance_criteria.When: The system extracts fields from positions 1 through 3 of the message
acceptance_criteria.Then: The following transaction identity fields must be populated from the message in positional order: Authorization Date (position 1), Authorization Time (position 2), and Card Number (position 3)

rules.rule_name: Extract Transaction Type Classification Fields from Authorization Request
rules.rule_description: Defines the extraction of five transaction classification and type fields from positions 4 through 8 of the comma-delimited authorization request message. These fields describe the nature, origin, and processing characteristics of the authorization request.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:

─────────────────────────
Authorization Type
Card Expiry Date

acceptance_criteria.Given: A comma-delimited authorization request message has been received and is being parsed
acceptance_criteria.When: The system extracts fields from positions 4 through 8 of the message
acceptance_criteria.Then: The following transaction type fields must be populated from the message in positional order: Authorization Type (position 4), Card Expiry Date (position 5), Message Type (position 6), Message Source (position 7), and Processing Code (position 8)

rules.rule_name: Extract Transaction Amount as Text String from Authorization Request
rules.rule_description: Defines the extraction of the Transaction Amount from position 9 of the comma-delimited authorization request message. The amount is initially extracted as a text string because it is embedded in a text-based message format and requires a subsequent conversion step before it can be used in financial calculations.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:

Transaction Amount
as Text String

acceptance_criteria.Given: A comma-delimited authorization request message has been received and is being parsed
acceptance_criteria.When: The system extracts the field at position 9 of the message
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Transaction Amount must be extracted and stored as a text string value in a temporary alphanumeric holding field, ready for subsequent numeric conversion before any financial calculations are performed

rules.rule_name: Extract Merchant Details from Authorization Request
rules.rule_description: Defines the extraction of eight merchant and transaction channel fields from positions 10 through 17 of the comma-delimited authorization request message. These fields identify the merchant, their location, the country of the acquiring bank, and how the card was presented at the point of sale.

acceptance_criteria.When: The system extracts fields from positions 10 through 17 of the message

rules.rule_name: Transaction Amount Extraction from Comma-Delimited Request Message

rules.sub_graph_node_text: Receive Transaction Amount as Alphanumeric Text String from Parsed Request Message

acceptance_criteria.Given: An authorization request message has been received from the request queue as a comma-delimited text string containing 18 fields: Authorization Date, Authorization Time, Card Number, Authorization Type, Card Expiry Date, Message Type, Message Source, Processing Code, Transaction Amount, Merchant Category Code, Acquirer Country Code, POS Entry Mode, Merchant ID, Merchant Name, Merchant City, Merchant State, Merchant ZIP, and Transaction ID
acceptance_criteria.When: The system parses the full request message by splitting on comma delimiters to extract each individual field into its corresponding data element
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Transaction Amount is extracted as an alphanumeric text string into the working storage field WS-TRANSACTION-AMT-AN, representing the 9th positional field in the comma-delimited message, ready for subsequent numeric conversion

rules.rule_name: Alphanumeric Transaction Amount Conversion to Numeric Value
rules.rule_description: The transaction amount extracted from the request message is in alphanumeric text format (e.g., '1234.56') and must be converted to a true numeric value before it can be used in arithmetic calculations such as available credit comparison.

acceptance_criteria.When: The system applies a numeric value conversion function (NUMVAL) to the alphanumeric transaction amount string
acceptance_criteria.Then: The alphanumeric text string is converted to its equivalent numeric value (e.g., '1234.56' becomes the numeric value 1234.56) and stored in the authorization request transaction amount field PA-RQ-TRANSACTION-AMT, which is capable of supporting arithmetic operations

rules.rule_name: Converted Numeric Transaction Amount Stored for Authorization Decision and Response

acceptance_criteria.Given: The transaction amount has been successfully converted from alphanumeric text format to a numeric value and is held in the authorization request field PA-RQ-TRANSACTION-AMT
acceptance_criteria.When: The system stores the converted numeric transaction amount into the working storage amount field WS-TRANSACTION-AMT
acceptance_criteria.Then: The numeric transaction amount is available in WS-TRANSACTION-AMT for use in the authorization decision process, specifically for comparison against the available credit amount to determine approval or decline, and for inclusion in the authorization response message

rules.rule_name: Card Number Lookup in Cross-Reference File
rules.rule_description: When an authorization request is received, the card number from the request must be looked up in the Card Cross-Reference (CCXREF) file to determine whether the card is known to the system and to retrieve its linked account and customer identifiers.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Look Up Card Number in Card Cross-Reference File CCXREF

acceptance_criteria.Given: An authorization request has been received containing a Card Number
acceptance_criteria.When: The system performs a lookup of the Card Number in the Card Cross-Reference (CCXREF) file
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system retrieves the full Card Cross-Reference record associated with that Card Number, which contains the linked Account ID and Customer ID

rules.rule_name: Card Found in Cross-Reference — Retrieve Account and Customer IDs
rules.rule_description: When the card number is successfully located in the Card Cross-Reference file, the system marks the card as found and makes the associated Account ID and Customer ID available for subsequent account and customer record retrieval steps.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Card Record Found - Retrieve Associated Account ID and Customer ID

acceptance_criteria.Given: A lookup of the Card Number has been performed against the Card Cross-Reference (CCXREF) file
acceptance_criteria.When: The Card Number is found in the CCXREF file
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the Card Found flag to TRUE and the Card Cross-Reference record — containing the associated Account ID and Customer ID — is made available for subsequent processing steps including account record retrieval, customer record retrieval, and authorization summary retrieval

rules.rule_name: Card Not Found in Cross-Reference — Flag and Log Warning
rules.rule_description: When the card number submitted in the authorization request does not exist in the Card Cross-Reference file, the system must flag the card as not found, flag the account as not found, and log a business warning event identifying the card number that could not be located.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Card Not Found - Mark Card as Not Found - Log Warning Event

acceptance_criteria.Given: A lookup of the Card Number has been performed against the Card Cross-Reference (CCXREF) file
acceptance_criteria.When: The Card Number is NOT found in the CCXREF file
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the Card Not Found in Cross-Reference flag to TRUE, sets the Account Not Found in Master flag to TRUE, and logs a warning event with: Event Location Code = 'A001', Severity = Warning, Category = Application, Message = 'CARD NOT FOUND IN XREF', and the Card Number recorded as the event key

rules.rule_name: Card Found Flag Controls Downstream Data Retrieval
rules.rule_description: The Card Found flag, set during the cross-reference lookup, acts as the control gate that determines whether the system proceeds to retrieve account, customer, authorization summary, and profile data. If the card was not found, these retrieval steps are bypassed entirely.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Card Found Flag Set?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Card Cross-Reference lookup has completed and the Card Found flag has been evaluated
acceptance_criteria.When: The Card Found flag is TRUE (card was located in CCXREF with a valid Account ID and Customer ID)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system proceeds to perform all four downstream data retrieval steps in sequence: (1) Account Master Record retrieval, (2) Customer Master Record retrieval, (3) Pending Authorization Summary retrieval, and (4) Profile Data retrieval; if the Card Found flag is FALSE, all four retrieval steps are skipped

rules.rule_name: Decline Reason Code Assignment for Card Not Found
rules.rule_description: When the authorization decision results in a decline and the root cause is that the card, account, or customer could not be found in the system, the decline reason code 3100 is assigned to the response to communicate to the requester that the card is not linked to any known account or customer.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Proceed to Authorization Decision - Decline with Reason 3100 - Card Not Found

acceptance_criteria.Given: The authorization decision has resulted in a DECLINE outcome
acceptance_criteria.When: The decline was caused by any of the following conditions: (1) Card Number was not found in the Card Cross-Reference file, OR (2) Account was not found in the Account Master, OR (3) Customer was not found in the Customer Master
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system assigns Authorization Response Reason Code = '3100' to the response message, indicating the card is not linked to a recognized account or customer in the system

rules.rule_name: Authorization Database Write Restricted to Known Cards
rules.rule_description: Authorization records — both the summary and the detail — are only written to the database when the card number was successfully found in the Card Cross-Reference file. Transactions for unknown cards do not generate any database records beyond the decline response.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Card Found Flag Set?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The authorization decision has been made and the response has been sent to the requester
acceptance_criteria.When: The Card Found in Cross-Reference flag is TRUE
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system proceeds to write the authorization results to the database, including updating or inserting the Authorization Summary record and inserting the Authorization Detail record; if the Card Found flag is FALSE, no authorization records are written to the database

rules.rule_name: Account Record Lookup Using Cross-Reference Account ID
rules.rule_description: When processing an authorization request, the system must use the Account ID obtained from the Card Cross-Reference file to look up the corresponding account master record in the Account Master File (ACCTDAT), which contains credit limit, current balance, cash credit limit, and account status details.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Use Account ID obtained from Card Cross-Reference Lookup

acceptance_criteria.Given: A card has been successfully found in the Card Cross-Reference file, and an Account ID has been retrieved from that cross-reference record
acceptance_criteria.When: The system initiates the account record retrieval step of the authorization process
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must use the Account ID from the Card Cross-Reference record as the lookup key to read the Account Master File (ACCTDAT) and retrieve the full account record including credit limit, current balance, cash credit limit, and account status

rules.rule_name: Successful Account Record Retrieval
rules.rule_description: When the account master record is successfully found and retrieved using the Account ID from the cross-reference, the system marks the account as found and makes the account details available for subsequent authorization decision-making, including credit limit, current balance, cash credit limit, and account status.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Account Record Retrieved Successfully / Account Details Now Available: Credit Limit, Current Balance, Cash Credit Limit, Account Status

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has used the Account ID from the Card Cross-Reference to look up the Account Master File (ACCTDAT)
acceptance_criteria.When: The account record is found and successfully read from the Account Master File
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must mark the account status as 'Found in Account Master' and make the following account details available for the authorization decision: Account Credit Limit, Account Current Balance, Account Cash Credit Limit, and Account Status

rules.rule_name: Account Record Not Found in Account Master
rules.rule_description: When the account record cannot be found in the Account Master File using the Account ID from the cross-reference, the system must mark the account as not found and log a business warning, after which the authorization process proceeds toward a decline decision due to missing account data.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Mark Account as Not Found / Log Warning: Account Not Found in Account Master

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has used the Account ID from the Card Cross-Reference to look up the Account Master File (ACCTDAT)
acceptance_criteria.When: No account record is found in the Account Master File for the given Account ID
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must: (1) Mark the account status as 'Account Not Found in Master', (2) Log a business warning with the message 'ACCT NOT FOUND IN XREF' along with the Account ID as the event key, and (3) Proceed toward a decline decision for the authorization request due to missing account information

rules.rule_name: Account Master File Read Failure Halts Processing
rules.rule_description: When an unexpected error occurs while attempting to read the Account Master File (other than a record not found condition), the system must log a critical error with full error details and immediately halt all further authorization processing for the current execution cycle.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Log Critical Error: Failed to Read Account Master File / End: Halt Processing

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has used the Account ID from the Card Cross-Reference to look up the Account Master File (ACCTDAT)
acceptance_criteria.When: An unexpected error occurs while reading the Account Master File — meaning the result is neither a successful read nor a record-not-found condition
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must: (1) Log a critical error with the message 'FAILED TO READ ACCT FILE', the Account ID as the event key, and the associated error response codes for diagnosis, (2) Classify the error as a critical application failure, and (3) Immediately halt all further authorization processing — no further messages are processed in the current execution cycle

rules.rule_name: Retrieve Customer Master Record Using Cross-Reference Customer ID
rules.rule_description: The system must use the Customer ID obtained from the Card Cross-Reference lookup to retrieve the corresponding customer profile from the Customer Master file. This establishes the link between the card presented for authorization and the customer who owns the account.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Use Customer ID obtained from Card Cross-Reference Lookup

acceptance_criteria.Given: A card authorization request is being processed and the Card Cross-Reference lookup has been successfully completed, yielding a Customer ID associated with the presented card number
acceptance_criteria.When: The system initiates the customer profile retrieval step
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Customer ID from the Card Cross-Reference record must be used as the lookup key to read the Customer Master file (CUSTDAT), and the full customer profile record must be retrieved into the customer record area for use in subsequent authorization processing

rules.rule_name: Customer Master Record Successfully Retrieved
rules.rule_description: When the Customer Master record is found in the Customer Master file using the Customer ID from the cross-reference, the system marks the customer as found and continues with the authorization process using the retrieved customer profile data.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Customer Profile Information successfully retrieved

acceptance_criteria.Given: A customer record lookup has been initiated using the Customer ID obtained from the Card Cross-Reference record
acceptance_criteria.When: The Customer Master file (CUSTDAT) returns a matching record for the provided Customer ID
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must mark the customer status as 'Found in Master' (FOUND-CUST-IN-MSTR = TRUE) and continue with the authorization decision process using the retrieved customer profile information

rules.rule_name: Customer Master Record Not Found — Log Warning and Continue
rules.rule_description: When the Customer Master record cannot be found in the Customer Master file for the Customer ID obtained from the cross-reference, the system must flag the customer as not found, log a business warning event identifying the missing customer, and continue processing toward a decline decision rather than terminating the transaction abruptly.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Customer Record Not Found
Log Warning and Continue

acceptance_criteria.Given: A customer record lookup has been initiated using the Customer ID obtained from the Card Cross-Reference record
acceptance_criteria.When: The Customer Master file (CUSTDAT) does not contain a record matching the provided Customer ID
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must: (1) mark the customer status as 'Not Found in Master' (NFOUND-CUST-IN-MSTR = TRUE), (2) log a business warning event with error location code 'A003', warning severity level, application error category, error message 'CUST NOT FOUND IN XREF', and the Customer ID as the event key, and (3) continue processing — the transaction will proceed to the authorization decision step where it will be evaluated for decline

rules.rule_name: Authorization Declined Due to Customer Not Found in Master
rules.rule_description: When the customer record was not found in the Customer Master file during the authorization process, the authorization decision step must decline the transaction and assign the specific decline reason code indicating that the card, account, or customer data could not be located in the system.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Customer Not Found
Continue with Decline Processing

acceptance_criteria.Given: The customer record lookup during authorization processing resulted in the customer not being found in the Customer Master file (NFOUND-CUST-IN-MSTR = TRUE), and the authorization decision step has determined that the transaction must be declined
acceptance_criteria.When: The system assigns the decline reason code during the authorization decision
acceptance_criteria.Then: The authorization response must be set to declined with response code '05', approved amount of zero, and decline reason code '3100' (indicating Card, Account, or Customer data not found in the system), and this reason code and response must be included in the authorization response message sent back to the requester

rules.rule_name: Use Account ID as Search Key for Pending Authorization Summary Lookup
rules.rule_description: The Account ID retrieved from the Card Cross-Reference record must be used as the unique search key to locate the Pending Authorization Summary record in the IMS database.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Use Account ID obtained from Card Cross-Reference as search key

acceptance_criteria.Given: A card authorization request has been received and the Card Cross-Reference record has been successfully retrieved, providing a valid Account ID linked to the card number
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares to query the Pending Authorization Summary database
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Account ID obtained from the Card Cross-Reference record must be set as the search key (ACCNTID) used to query the Pending Authorization Summary segment (PAUTSUM0) in the IMS database

rules.rule_name: Query IMS Database for Pending Authorization Summary Record
rules.rule_description: The system must perform a direct retrieval query against the IMS Pending Authorization Summary segment (PAUTSUM0) using the Account ID to determine whether an existing pending authorization summary exists for the account.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Query IMS Database for Pending Authorization Summary record matching the Account ID

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account ID from the Card Cross-Reference has been set as the search key
acceptance_criteria.When: The system executes a Get Unique (GU) query against the IMS Pending Authorization Summary segment (PAUTSUM0) using the Account ID as the search criterion
acceptance_criteria.Then: The IMS database returns either the matching Pending Authorization Summary record, a not-found status indicating no summary exists for the account, or an error status indicating the query could not be completed

rules.rule_name: Retrieve Pending Authorization Summary Data When Record Found
rules.rule_description: When a Pending Authorization Summary record is found in the IMS database for the account, the system retrieves all current pending authorization data including balances, limits, and authorization counts to be used in the available credit calculation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Retrieve Current Pending Authorization Summary:
- Credit Balance
- Cash Balance
- Credit Limit
- Cash Limit
- Approved Auth Count
- Approved Auth Amount
- Declined Auth Count
- Declined Auth Amount

acceptance_criteria.Given: A query has been executed against the IMS Pending Authorization Summary segment (PAUTSUM0) using the Account ID
acceptance_criteria.When: The IMS database successfully locates and returns a matching Pending Authorization Summary record for the Account ID
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system retrieves the complete Pending Authorization Summary record containing: Credit Balance, Cash Balance, Credit Limit, Cash Credit Limit, Approved Authorization Count, Approved Authorization Amount, Declined Authorization Count, and Declined Authorization Amount — and marks the summary status as FOUND (FOUND-PAUT-SMRY-SEG) to indicate that this data is available for the available credit calculation

rules.rule_name: Mark Pending Authorization Summary as Not Found When No Record Exists
rules.rule_description: When no Pending Authorization Summary record exists in the IMS database for the account, the system marks the summary as not found, indicating this is either a new account or an account with no prior pending authorizations in the system.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Mark Summary as NOT FOUND
No existing pending authorizations for account

acceptance_criteria.Given: A query has been executed against the IMS Pending Authorization Summary segment (PAUTSUM0) using the Account ID
acceptance_criteria.When: The IMS database returns a segment-not-found status, indicating no Pending Authorization Summary record exists for the given Account ID
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system marks the pending authorization summary status as NOT FOUND (NFOUND-PAUT-SMRY-SEG), indicating that no existing pending authorizations exist for this account, and processing continues without raising an error or warning

rules.rule_name: Fall Back to Account Master Data for Available Credit Calculation When Summary Not Found
rules.rule_description: When no Pending Authorization Summary record is found for the account, the available credit calculation must fall back to using the Account Master record data (Account Credit Limit and Account Current Balance) instead of the pending authorization summary data.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Available Credit Calculation will use Account Master Record data instead

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Pending Authorization Summary query has completed and the summary record was NOT FOUND for the account, AND the Account Master record was successfully retrieved
acceptance_criteria.When: The system proceeds to calculate the available credit amount for the authorization decision
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system uses the Account Master record data — specifically Account Credit Limit and Account Current Balance — as the basis for the available credit calculation, rather than the Pending Authorization Summary credit limit and credit balance

rules.rule_name: Proceed to Available Credit Calculation After Summary Retrieval Attempt
rules.rule_description: Regardless of whether the Pending Authorization Summary record was found or not found, the system must always proceed to the available credit calculation step. The outcome of the summary retrieval (found or not found) determines which data source is used for the calculation, but does not stop the authorization process.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: End: Proceed to Available Credit Calculation

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Pending Authorization Summary retrieval query has completed with either a FOUND or NOT FOUND result
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the result of the Pending Authorization Summary query
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system proceeds to the authorization decision step (6000-MAKE-DECISION) in both cases — if the summary was FOUND, the pending authorization summary data (Credit Limit and Credit Balance) is used for available credit calculation; if the summary was NOT FOUND, the Account Master data (Account Credit Limit and Account Current Balance) is used instead — and the authorization decision process continues without interruption
