rules.rule_name: Capture Error Timestamp for Log Entry
rules.rule_description: When any error or warning event is detected, the system must capture the current date and time to accurately timestamp the error log entry before recording it.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Capture Current Date and Time for Error Timestamp

acceptance_criteria.Given: An error or warning event has been detected during authorization processing (e.g., queue open failure, file read failure, IMS failure, or a business data warning such as card not found)
acceptance_criteria.When: The error logging process is initiated
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system captures the current date in YYMMDD format and the current time, which will be used as the timestamp on the error log record

rules.rule_name: Populate Error Log Record with Transaction and Program Identity
rules.rule_description: Each error log entry must be stamped with the identity of the transaction and program that encountered the error, enabling traceability back to the originating process.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Populate Error Log Record with Transaction ID and Program Name

acceptance_criteria.Given: The current date and time have been captured for the error log entry
acceptance_criteria.When: The error log record is being assembled
acceptance_criteria.Then: The error log record is populated with: the current CICS Transaction ID recorded as the Application identifier, the Authorization Program name recorded as the Program identifier, the captured current date recorded as the Error Date, and the captured current time recorded as the Error Time

rules.rule_name: Populate Error Log Record with Error Details and Affected Business Entity
rules.rule_description: Each error log entry must contain sufficient detail to identify where the error occurred, what the error was, and which business entity (e.g., card number or account ID) was being processed at the time, enabling business and operations teams to investigate and resolve issues.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Add Error Details to Log Record: Error Location Code, Error Code 1 and Error Code 2, Descriptive Error Message, Affected Event Key e.g. Card Number

acceptance_criteria.Given: An error or warning event has been detected and the log record identity fields have been populated
acceptance_criteria.When: The error details are added to the log record
acceptance_criteria.Then: The error log record must include all of the following: an Error Location Code identifying the specific point in processing where the error occurred (e.g., 'M001' for MQ queue open failure, 'M003' for MQ read failure, 'M004' for MQ reply send failure, 'C001'/'C002'/'C003' for file read failures on XREF/Account/Customer files, 'A001' for card not found in cross-reference, 'A002' for account not found, 'A003' for customer not found, 'I001' for IMS PSB schedule failure, 'I002' for IMS authorization summary read failure, 'I003' for IMS authorization summary update failure, 'I004' for IMS authorization detail insert failure); an Error Severity classification of either Critical or Warning; an Error Type classification identifying the system component involved (MQ messaging system, CICS file system, IMS database, or Application business data); a primary Error Code (Error Code 1) containing the system completion code where applicable; a secondary Error Code (Error Code 2) containing the system reason code where applicable; a descriptive Error Message in plain text describing the nature of the failure (e.g., 'REQ MQ OPEN ERROR', 'FAILED TO READ REQUEST MQ', 'FAILED TO PUT ON REPLY MQ', 'FAILED TO READ XREF FILE', 'FAILED TO READ ACCT FILE', 'FAILED TO READ CUST FILE', 'IMS SCHD FAILED', 'IMS GET SUMMARY FAILED', 'IMS UPDATE SUMRY FAILED', 'IMS INSERT DETL FAILED', 'CARD NOT FOUND IN XREF', 'ACCT NOT FOUND IN XREF', 'CUST NOT FOUND IN XREF'); and the Affected Event Key identifying the business entity being processed at the time of the error, such as the Card Number or Account ID

rules.rule_name: Write Error Log Record to System Error Log Queue
rules.rule_description: Once the error log record is fully assembled with all required details, it must be written to the centralized system error log queue (CSSL) to ensure the error is permanently recorded for operational monitoring and audit purposes.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Write Error Log Record to System Error Log Queue

acceptance_criteria.Given: The error log record has been fully populated with timestamp, transaction identity, program identity, error location code, error severity, error type, error codes, descriptive message, and affected business entity key
acceptance_criteria.When: The error log record is ready to be persisted
acceptance_criteria.Then: The complete error log record is written to the System Error Log Queue named 'CSSL', and the full length of the error log record is written ensuring no data is truncated

rules.rule_name: Classify Error Severity as Critical or Warning
rules.rule_description: After the error log record has been written, the system must evaluate the severity of the error to determine whether processing can safely continue or must be immediately terminated. This classification drives the subsequent processing path.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is this a Critical Error?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The error log record has been successfully written to the System Error Log Queue
acceptance_criteria.When: The error severity is evaluated
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the error was classified as Critical (ERR-CRITICAL flag is set), the system must immediately initiate program termination by releasing all open resources and ending the program; if the error was classified as Warning only (ERR-CRITICAL flag is not set), the system continues processing with the next step without interruption

rules.rule_name: Continue Processing After Warning Event
rules.rule_description: Warning-level events represent non-fatal business data conditions (such as a card not found in the cross-reference, an account not found, or a customer not found) that are logged for visibility but do not prevent the authorization decision process from continuing.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Warning Logged - Processing Continues with Next Step

acceptance_criteria.Given: An error event has been detected, logged to the System Error Log Queue, and evaluated as a Warning severity (not Critical)
acceptance_criteria.When: The severity check determines the error is Warning only
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program resumes normal processing flow from the point after the error logging call, allowing the authorization decision and response steps to proceed; the warning conditions that trigger this path include: card number not found in the Card Cross-Reference file (location A001), account not found in the Account Master file (location A002), and customer not found in the Customer Master file (location A003)

rules.rule_name: Terminate All Open Resources on Critical Error
rules.rule_description: When a critical error is encountered, the program must safely release all open system resources — including the IMS database session and the MQ message queue connection — before ending, to prevent resource leaks and ensure system integrity.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Terminate All Open Resources IMS PSB Session and MQ Queue Connections

acceptance_criteria.Given: A critical error has been detected and logged, and the severity check has determined that the program must terminate
acceptance_criteria.When: The program termination sequence is initiated
acceptance_criteria.Then: The following resource cleanup steps are performed in order: first, if an IMS PSB (Program Specification Block) database session was successfully scheduled and is currently active, it is formally terminated to release the IMS database session; second, if the Request MQ Queue was successfully opened and is currently open, it is formally closed to release the MQ queue connection; after all open resources have been released, the program ends immediately and returns control to the calling system, with no further authorization messages processed in the current execution cycle

key_functionalities.title: Critical Error Handling
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([Critical Error Detected]) --> B[Log Error Event\nRecord timestamp, program name,\ntransaction ID, error location,\nerror codes and description]
    B --> C{Is Error\nCritical?}

    C -->|Yes - Critical| E{Is IMS PSB\nCurrently Active?}
    E -->|Yes| F[Terminate IMS PSB Session\nRelease all IMS database\nresources and connections]
    F --> G{Is MQ Request\nQueue Open?}
    E -->|No| G
    G -->|Yes| H[Close MQ Request Queue\nRelease message queue\nconnection and resources]
    H --> I([End Program Execution])
    G -->|No| I

rules.rule_name: Log Error Event with Full Audit Details
rules.rule_description: When any error condition is detected during authorization processing, the system must capture and record a complete error event including the current date and time, the application transaction identifier, the program name, the error location code, error codes, and a descriptive error message to the error log.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Log Error Event
Record timestamp, program name,
transaction ID, error location,
error codes and description

acceptance_criteria.Given: An error condition has been detected during authorization processing, and the error record has been populated with: error location code (e.g., 'A001', 'C001', 'M001', 'I001', etc.), error type (Critical or Warning), error category (Application, CICS, MQ, or IMS), one or two error codes, an error message description, and optionally an event key (e.g., card number or account ID)
acceptance_criteria.When: The error logging routine is invoked
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must: (1) capture the current date (in YYMMDD format) and current time, (2) record the application transaction ID as the application identifier, (3) record the program name, (4) populate the error log record with the current date and time, (5) write the complete error log record — containing application ID, program name, date, time, error location, error type, error category, error codes, error message, and event key — to the error log destination

rules.rule_name: Classify Error Severity and Route Processing
rules.rule_description: After logging an error event, the system must evaluate the severity of the error to determine whether processing can continue or must be immediately terminated. Warning-level errors allow processing to continue, while critical errors trigger an immediate termination sequence.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Is Error
Critical?

acceptance_criteria.Given: An error event has been logged with a severity classification of either Critical or Warning
acceptance_criteria.When: The error severity is evaluated after the error log has been written
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the error is classified as a Warning, processing continues normally with no interruption; if the error is classified as Critical, the system immediately invokes the termination sequence to release all active resources and end program execution

rules.rule_name: Initiate Full Resource Cleanup on Critical Error
rules.rule_description: When a critical error is detected, the system must initiate a controlled termination sequence that ensures all active resources — including IMS database sessions and MQ message queue connections — are properly released before the program ends.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Is Error
Critical?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A critical error has been detected and logged during authorization processing
acceptance_criteria.When: The critical error termination sequence is triggered
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must execute the full resource cleanup routine (closing IMS PSB and MQ connections as applicable) and then end program execution

rules.rule_name: Terminate Active IMS Database Session on Shutdown
rules.rule_description: During the termination sequence, the system must check whether an IMS Program Specification Block (PSB) session is currently active. If it is, the IMS session must be formally terminated to release all IMS database resources before the program ends.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:

acceptance_criteria.Given: The termination sequence has been initiated, either due to a critical error or normal end of processing
acceptance_criteria.When: The system checks whether an IMS PSB session is currently scheduled and active
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the IMS PSB session is active, the system must issue a formal IMS TERM command to release all IMS database resources and connections; if the IMS PSB session is not active, this step is skipped and processing continues to the next cleanup step

rules.rule_name: Close MQ Request Queue on Shutdown
rules.rule_description: During the termination sequence, the system must check whether the MQ Request Queue is currently open. If it is, the queue must be formally closed to release the message queue connection and resources. If the close operation itself fails, a warning is logged but the program still proceeds to end.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:

Close MQ Request Queue
Release message queue

acceptance_criteria.Given: The termination sequence is in progress and the IMS PSB cleanup step has been completed (or skipped)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system checks whether the MQ Request Queue is currently open
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the MQ Request Queue is open, the system must issue a formal close command to release the queue connection and resources; if the close is successful, the queue is marked as closed; if the close fails, a Warning-level MQ error is logged with the error location code 'M005', both the completion code and reason code, and the message 'FAILED TO CLOSE REQUEST MQ' — and processing continues to program end; if the MQ Request Queue was not open, this step is skipped entirely

rules.rule_name: End Program Execution After Resource Cleanup
rules.rule_description: After all active resources have been released (IMS PSB terminated and MQ queue closed as applicable), the program must formally end execution and return control, ensuring no further authorization processing occurs.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: End Program Execution

acceptance_criteria.Given: All active resources have been released — IMS PSB session terminated if it was active, and MQ Request Queue closed if it was open — as part of either a critical error termination or normal end-of-processing
acceptance_criteria.When: The resource cleanup sequence has completed
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program must formally end execution and return control, preventing any further authorization message processing

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program is started by a CICS trigger monitor with a trigger message containing the MQ queue name and trigger data
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program initializes and retrieves the trigger message from CICS
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The MQ request queue name is set from the trigger message queue name field, the trigger data is captured from the trigger message trigger data field, and the message wait interval is set to 5000 milliseconds for all subsequent queue read operations

all_rules.Rule_Name: Program Initialization via CICS Trigger Data Retrieval
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the program is triggered by a CICS trigger monitor, it retrieves the trigger message to identify the MQ request queue name and trigger data, and sets the message wait interval for subsequent queue reads.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The MQ request queue name has been retrieved from the CICS trigger data
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program attempts to open the MQ request queue
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The queue is opened in shared input mode; if the queue opens successfully, the queue is marked as open and processing continues; if the queue fails to open, a critical MQ error is logged with error location 'M001', error codes capturing the completion code and reason code, and the message 'REQ MQ OPEN ERROR', and the program terminates immediately

all_rules.Rule_Name: MQ Request Queue Open in Shared Input Mode
all_rules.Rule_Description: The program opens the MQ request queue in shared input mode using the queue name retrieved from the trigger data, allowing multiple consumers to read from the same queue concurrently.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The MQ request queue is open and the program is ready to process authorization requests
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program attempts to read the next message from the MQ request queue with a wait interval of 5000 milliseconds
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If a message is successfully retrieved, the message correlation ID is saved and the reply-to queue name is captured for later response routing; if no message is available, the no-more-messages flag is set and the processing loop ends; if a read error occurs, a critical error is logged with error location 'M003', completion code, reason code, and the message 'FAILED TO READ REQUEST MQ' along with the card number as the event key, and the program terminates immediately

all_rules.Rule_Name: Authorization Request Message Read from MQ Queue
all_rules.Rule_Description: The program reads the next available authorization request message from the MQ request queue, capturing the correlation ID and reply-to queue name needed to route the response back to the requester.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A raw authorization request message has been successfully read from the MQ request queue
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program parses the comma-delimited message content
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The following 18 fields are extracted in order: Authorization Date, Authorization Time, Card Number, Authorization Type, Card Expiry Date, Message Type, Message Source, Processing Code, Transaction Amount (as alphanumeric string), Merchant Category Code, Acquirer Country Code, POS Entry Mode, Merchant ID, Merchant Name, Merchant City, Merchant State, Merchant ZIP, and Transaction ID

all_rules.Rule_Name: Authorization Request Message Parsing
all_rules.Rule_Description: Each authorization request message is a comma-delimited string that must be parsed into its individual data fields covering card details, transaction information, and merchant information.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The transaction amount has been extracted from the request message as an alphanumeric string
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program converts the transaction amount for use in authorization processing
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The alphanumeric transaction amount string is converted to a numeric value using the NUMVAL function, and the resulting numeric transaction amount is stored for use in credit availability and authorization decision calculations

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transaction Amount Conversion from Alphanumeric to Numeric
all_rules.Rule_Description: The transaction amount arrives in the request message as an alphanumeric string and must be converted to a numeric value before it can be used in credit availability calculations.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program needs to access IMS database segments for authorization processing
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program schedules the IMS PSB
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the PSB is not already scheduled, it is scheduled normally; if the PSB was already scheduled from a previous iteration, it is first terminated and then rescheduled; if scheduling succeeds, the IMS PSB scheduled flag is set to true; if scheduling fails, a critical IMS error is logged with error location 'I001', the IMS return code, and the message 'IMS SCHD FAILED', and the program terminates immediately

all_rules.Rule_Name: IMS PSB Scheduling for Database Access
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before accessing IMS database segments for pending authorization summary and detail records, the program must schedule the IMS Program Specification Block (PSB). If the PSB is already active from a prior cycle, it is terminated and rescheduled.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A card number has been extracted from the authorization request message
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program looks up the card number in the Card Cross-Reference (CCXREF) VSAM file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the card is found, the associated account ID and customer ID are retrieved and the card-found flag is set to true; if the card is not found, the card-not-found flag is set, the account-not-found flag is set, a warning is logged with error location 'A001', the message 'CARD NOT FOUND IN XREF', and the card number as the event key, and processing continues directly to the authorization decision without reading account or customer records; if a file access error occurs, a critical error is logged with error location 'C001', the response code, reason code, and the message 'FAILED TO READ XREF FILE' with the card number as the event key, and the program terminates immediately

all_rules.Rule_Name: Card Number Validation via Cross-Reference Lookup
all_rules.Rule_Description: Every authorization request must be validated by looking up the card number in the Card Cross-Reference file to retrieve the associated account ID and customer ID required for further processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The card number has been found in the Card Cross-Reference file and an account ID has been retrieved
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program reads the account master record from the Account Master (ACCTDAT) VSAM file using the account ID
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the account record is found, the account-found flag is set to true and the credit limit, current balance, and account details are available for authorization processing; if the account is not found, the account-not-found flag is set, a warning is logged with error location 'A002', the message 'ACCT NOT FOUND IN XREF', and the account ID as the event key; if a file access error occurs, a critical error is logged with error location 'C002', the response code, reason code, and the message 'FAILED TO READ ACCT FILE' with the account ID as the event key, and the program terminates immediately

all_rules.Rule_Name: Account Master Record Retrieval
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a card is found in the cross-reference, the associated account master record is retrieved using the account ID from the cross-reference to obtain the credit limit, current balance, and account status needed for authorization decisions.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The card number has been found in the Card Cross-Reference file and a customer ID has been retrieved
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program reads the customer master record from the Customer Master (CUSTDAT) VSAM file using the customer ID
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the customer record is found, the customer-found flag is set to true and customer profile information is available; if the customer is not found, the customer-not-found flag is set, a warning is logged with error location 'A003', the message 'CUST NOT FOUND IN XREF', and the customer ID as the event key; if a file access error occurs, a critical error is logged with error location 'C003', the response code, reason code, and the message 'FAILED TO READ CUST FILE' with the customer ID as the event key, and the program terminates immediately

all_rules.Rule_Name: Customer Master Record Retrieval
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a card is found in the cross-reference, the associated customer master record is retrieved using the customer ID from the cross-reference to obtain the customer profile information.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The account ID has been retrieved from the Card Cross-Reference file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program queries the IMS PAUTSUM0 segment for a pending authorization summary record matching the account ID
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the summary record is found, the pending-auth-summary-found flag is set to true and the credit limit and credit balance from the summary are available for available credit calculation; if no summary record exists for the account, the pending-auth-summary-not-found flag is set and the program will fall back to using the account master record for credit calculation; if an IMS access error occurs, a critical error is logged with error location 'I002', the IMS return code, and the message 'IMS GET SUMMARY FAILED' with the card number as the event key, and the program terminates immediately

all_rules.Rule_Name: Pending Authorization Summary Retrieval from IMS
all_rules.Rule_Description: The program queries the IMS database for an existing pending authorization summary record for the account to obtain the most current credit limit and credit balance reflecting all previously approved but not yet settled authorizations.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A pending authorization summary record has been found in IMS for the account
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program calculates the available credit for the authorization decision
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The available credit amount is calculated as: Available Amount = Credit Limit (from Pending Auth Summary) minus Credit Balance (from Pending Auth Summary)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Available Credit Calculation Using Pending Authorization Summary
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a pending authorization summary record exists for the account, the available credit is calculated using the credit limit and credit balance from the IMS pending authorization summary, which reflects the most current state including all previously approved but unsettled authorizations.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: No pending authorization summary record exists in IMS for the account, but the account master record has been found
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program calculates the available credit for the authorization decision
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The available credit amount is calculated as: Available Amount = Account Credit Limit (from Account Master) minus Account Current Balance (from Account Master)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Available Credit Calculation Using Account Master as Fallback
all_rules.Rule_Description: When no pending authorization summary record exists for the account in IMS, the available credit is calculated using the credit limit and current balance from the account master record as a fallback.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The transaction amount and available credit amount have been determined
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program compares the transaction amount against the available credit
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the transaction amount is less than or equal to the available credit, the authorization is approved with response code '00' and the approved amount is set equal to the transaction amount; if the transaction amount exceeds the available credit, the authorization is declined with the insufficient-funds flag set, response code '05', approved amount set to zero, and decline reason code '4100'

all_rules.Rule_Name: Authorization Approval Decision Based on Available Credit
all_rules.Rule_Description: The core authorization decision compares the requested transaction amount against the calculated available credit to determine whether to approve or decline the transaction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The card was found in the cross-reference but neither a pending authorization summary nor an account master record exists for the account
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program evaluates the authorization decision
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The authorization is unconditionally declined with response code '05' and approved amount set to zero, as there is insufficient account data to evaluate the credit availability

all_rules.Rule_Name: Authorization Decline When No Account Data Exists
all_rules.Rule_Description: When neither a pending authorization summary nor an account master record can be found for the card, the transaction is unconditionally declined as there is no basis for credit evaluation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The card number from the authorization request was not found in the Card Cross-Reference file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program reaches the authorization decision step
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The authorization is declined with response code '05', approved amount set to zero, and decline reason code '3100' assigned to indicate the card, account, or customer was not found

all_rules.Rule_Name: Authorization Decline When Card Not Found in Cross-Reference
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the card number is not found in the Card Cross-Reference file, the transaction is declined without any credit evaluation, as the card cannot be associated with a valid account.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization has been declined
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program assigns the decline reason code
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The reason code is assigned based on the following priority: '3100' if the card was not found in the cross-reference, or the account was not found, or the customer was not found; '4100' if the decline was due to insufficient available credit; '4200' if the card is not active; '4300' if the account is closed; '5100' if the card is flagged for fraud; '5200' if the merchant is flagged for fraud; '9000' for any other unspecified decline reason; if the authorization is approved, the reason code is set to '0000'

all_rules.Rule_Name: Decline Reason Code Assignment
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an authorization is declined, a specific reason code is assigned to explain the cause of the decline, enabling the requester to understand and communicate the reason to the cardholder.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The authorization decision has been made with all response fields populated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program builds the authorization response message
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: A comma-delimited response message is constructed containing the following six fields in order: Card Number, Transaction ID, Authorization ID Code (set from the authorization time), Response Code ('00' for approved or '05' for declined), Authorization Response Reason Code ('0000' for approved or the specific decline reason code), and Approved Amount (equal to the transaction amount for approvals or zero for declines)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Authorization Response Message Construction
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the authorization decision is made, a comma-delimited response message is constructed containing all fields required by the requester to process the authorization outcome.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The authorization response message has been built and the reply-to queue name and correlation ID were captured from the original request message
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program sends the authorization response
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The response message is sent to the reply-to queue specified in the original request using the saved correlation ID to correlate the response to the original request; the message is sent as non-persistent with an expiry of 50 units and message type set to reply; if the send fails, a critical error is logged with error location 'M004', the completion code, reason code, and the message 'FAILED TO PUT ON REPLY MQ' with the card number as the event key, and the program terminates immediately

all_rules.Rule_Name: Authorization Response Delivery via MQ Reply Queue
all_rules.Rule_Description: The authorization response message is sent back to the requester through the MQ reply queue specified in the original request, correlated to the original request message to enable the requester to match the response.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The authorization has been approved and the card was found in the cross-reference
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program updates the pending authorization summary in IMS
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The credit limit and cash credit limit are refreshed from the account master record; the approved authorization count is incremented by 1; the approved authorization amount total is increased by the approved amount; the credit balance is increased by the approved amount; the cash balance is set to zero; if a summary record already existed it is replaced, if no summary record existed a new one is inserted with the account ID and customer ID from the cross-reference; if the IMS update or insert fails, a critical error is logged with error location 'I003', the IMS return code, and the message 'IMS UPDATE SUMRY FAILED' with the card number as the event key, and the program terminates immediately

all_rules.Rule_Name: Authorization Summary Update for Approved Transactions
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an authorization is approved, the pending authorization summary record in IMS is updated to reflect the new approved authorization, incrementing counts, updating the approved amount total, and increasing the credit balance.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The authorization has been declined and the card was found in the cross-reference
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program updates the pending authorization summary in IMS
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The credit limit and cash credit limit are refreshed from the account master record; the declined authorization count is incremented by 1; the declined authorization amount total is increased by the transaction amount; if a summary record already existed it is replaced, if no summary record existed a new one is inserted with the account ID and customer ID from the cross-reference; if the IMS update or insert fails, a critical error is logged with error location 'I003', the IMS return code, and the message 'IMS UPDATE SUMRY FAILED' with the card number as the event key, and the program terminates immediately

all_rules.Rule_Name: Authorization Summary Update for Declined Transactions
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an authorization is declined, the pending authorization summary record in IMS is updated to track the declined authorization count and total declined amount for reporting and monitoring purposes.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The authorization summary has been updated and the card was found in the cross-reference
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program inserts the authorization detail record into IMS under the account's summary segment (PAUTDTL1 as child of PAUTSUM0)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: A new detail record is inserted containing: Authorization Date and Time, Card Number, Authorization Type, Card Expiry Date, Message Type, Message Source, Processing Code, Transaction Amount, Merchant Category Code, Acquirer Country Code, POS Entry Mode, Merchant ID, Merchant Name, Merchant City, Merchant State, Merchant ZIP, Transaction ID, Authorization ID Code, Response Code, Response Reason Code, and Approved Amount; the authorization status is set to 'PENDING MATCH' for approved transactions or 'AUTH DECLINED' for declined transactions; the fraud flag and fraud report date are initialized to blank; if the IMS insert fails, a critical error is logged with error location 'I004', the IMS return code, and the message 'IMS INSERT DETL FAILED' with the card number as the event key, and the program terminates immediately

all_rules.Rule_Name: Authorization Detail Record Insertion into IMS
all_rules.Rule_Description: A complete authorization detail record is inserted into IMS as a child segment under the account's authorization summary, capturing all transaction, merchant, and response details for audit and settlement purposes.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The authorization decision has been made and the program is preparing to write the detail record to IMS
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program generates the authorization timestamp
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current date is captured in YYDDD format and the current time is captured with millisecond precision; a reverse chronological sort key for the date is computed as 99999 minus the current YYDDD date; a reverse chronological sort key for the time is computed as 999999999 minus the current time including milliseconds; these complement values are stored in the authorization detail record so that the most recent authorization appears first when records are retrieved in ascending key order

all_rules.Rule_Name: Authorization Timestamp Generation with Reverse Chronological Sort Key
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before inserting the authorization detail record, a precise timestamp is generated and complement values are computed for the date and time fields to enable reverse chronological retrieval of authorization history.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization request has been fully processed with the decision made, response sent to the requester, and all IMS database updates completed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program issues a syncpoint
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All database updates for the current authorization (summary update and detail insert) are permanently committed; the IMS PSB scheduled flag is reset to not-scheduled so that a fresh PSB will be obtained for the next authorization message

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transaction Commit After Each Authorization
all_rules.Rule_Description: After each authorization request is fully processed — including the decision, response sent, and all database updates — a commit point is issued to permanently save all changes, ensuring each authorization is independently committed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization message has been fully processed and committed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program evaluates whether to continue processing
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the number of messages processed exceeds the configured processing limit, the loop-end flag is set and the program proceeds to termination; if the processing limit has not been reached, the program reads the next message from the MQ request queue and continues the processing loop

all_rules.Rule_Name: Message Processing Loop Control and Limit Enforcement
all_rules.Rule_Description: After each authorization is committed, the program checks whether the processing limit has been reached to decide whether to continue processing more messages or terminate the current execution cycle.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The message processing loop has ended either because no more messages are available or the processing limit has been reached
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program executes the termination sequence
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If an IMS PSB session is currently active, it is terminated; the MQ request queue close procedure is invoked to release the queue connection

all_rules.Rule_Name: Program Termination and Resource Cleanup
all_rules.Rule_Description: When all messages have been processed or the processing limit is reached, the program performs an orderly termination by releasing all acquired resources.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The MQ request queue was successfully opened earlier in the program
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program closes the MQ request queue during termination
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the queue was opened, the MQCLOSE call is made to close the queue connection; if the close is successful, the queue is marked as closed; if the close fails, a warning (non-critical) error is logged with error location 'M005', the completion code, reason code, and the message 'FAILED TO CLOSE REQUEST MQ', and processing continues to program end

all_rules.Rule_Name: MQ Request Queue Close
all_rules.Rule_Description: As part of program termination, the MQ request queue connection is closed to release the queue resource.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An error or warning condition has been detected during authorization processing
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program logs the error
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current timestamp (date and time) is captured; the error log record is written to the CSSL transient data queue containing: the CICS transaction ID as the application identifier, the program name, the current date, the current time, the error location code, error codes, and the error message; if the error is classified as critical, the program immediately invokes the critical error handler to terminate; if the error is classified as a warning, processing continues after logging

all_rules.Rule_Name: Error Logging with Severity Classification
all_rules.Rule_Description: All errors and warnings encountered during processing are logged to the error log queue with full context information including timestamp, program identification, error location, error codes, and a descriptive message.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A critical error has been logged that prevents the program from continuing normal processing
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program executes the critical error handler
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program invokes the termination sequence to release all resources: if an IMS PSB session is active it is terminated, and if the MQ request queue is open it is closed; after resource cleanup the program ends immediately without processing any further authorization messages

all_rules.Rule_Name: Critical Error Handling and Forced Program Termination
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a critical error is encountered, the program performs an orderly shutdown by releasing all resources before terminating, ensuring no resources are left in an inconsistent state.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The authorization processing program has been started by a CICS trigger event
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program begins initialization and requests trigger data from CICS
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The trigger data containing the request queue name and trigger processing details is retrieved and made available for subsequent initialization steps

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retrieve Trigger Data from CICS at Program Startup
all_rules.Rule_Description: At program initialization, the system retrieves trigger data from CICS to identify the incoming authorization request queue and associated processing parameters.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has attempted to retrieve trigger data from CICS during initialization
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The CICS response is evaluated to determine if the retrieval completed normally
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the CICS response indicates a normal successful retrieval, the program proceeds to extract the request queue name and trigger data from the trigger message; if the response indicates any other condition (non-normal), the program bypasses queue name and trigger data extraction and proceeds directly to set the message wait interval using default settings

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate Successful Retrieval of Trigger Data
all_rules.Rule_Description: The program checks whether the CICS trigger data was successfully retrieved before attempting to extract queue name and trigger details. If retrieval was not successful, the program proceeds with default settings without setting queue name or trigger data from the trigger message.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The CICS trigger data has been successfully retrieved and contains a valid queue name
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program extracts the queue name from the trigger message data
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The request queue name is set from the queue name field (QNAME) of the trigger message, and this queue name will be used to open the authorization request queue in the next processing step

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Request Queue Name from Trigger Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: When trigger data is successfully retrieved, the authorization request queue name is extracted from the trigger message and stored for use in opening and reading the incoming authorization request queue.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The CICS trigger data has been successfully retrieved and contains trigger processing information
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program extracts the trigger data field from the trigger message
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The trigger data is set from the trigger data field (TRIGGERDATA) of the trigger message and stored for use during the authorization processing session

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Trigger Data for Authorization Processing
all_rules.Rule_Description: When trigger data is successfully retrieved, the trigger data field from the trigger message is captured and stored for use during the authorization processing cycle.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has attempted to retrieve trigger data from CICS during initialization
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The CICS response indicates the trigger data retrieval was not successful (non-normal response)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program does not update the request queue name or trigger data fields from the trigger message, and proceeds directly to set the message wait interval using the pre-configured default values already present in the program's working storage

all_rules.Rule_Name: Apply Default Processing Settings When Trigger Data Unavailable
all_rules.Rule_Description: When trigger data cannot be successfully retrieved from CICS, the program does not set the request queue name or trigger data from the trigger message, and instead proceeds with whatever default queue name and processing parameters are already configured in the program.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program is completing its initialization phase, either after successfully extracting trigger data or after defaulting due to unsuccessful trigger data retrieval
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program sets the wait interval parameter for message queue reading operations
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The message wait interval is unconditionally set to 5000 milliseconds, meaning the program will wait up to 5 seconds for each authorization request message to arrive in the request queue before concluding no messages are available

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Message Wait Interval for Queue Reading
all_rules.Rule_Description: Regardless of whether trigger data was successfully retrieved or not, the program always sets the message wait interval to 5000 milliseconds. This interval controls how long the program will wait for an authorization request message to arrive in the queue before determining that no messages are available.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has been initialized and the authorization request queue name has been retrieved from the MQ trigger message and stored as the request queue name parameter
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to open the authorization request queue
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The target queue descriptor must be populated with the queue name from the initialization parameters, identifying the correct queue from which authorization request messages will be read

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Request Queue Name from Initialization Parameters
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before opening the authorization request queue, the system must configure the target queue identity using the queue name retrieved during program initialization from the MQ trigger message.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The request queue name has been set from initialization parameters and the queue descriptor has been configured with the correct queue name and queue type
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system attempts to open the authorization request queue using shared input access mode
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The queue open operation must be executed with shared input mode options, establishing a connection handle to the request queue that will be used for all subsequent message read operations

all_rules.Rule_Name: Open Authorization Request Queue in Shared Input Mode
all_rules.Rule_Description: The authorization request queue must be opened in shared input mode, allowing the program to read pending authorization request messages while permitting other consumers to access the same queue concurrently.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has attempted to open the authorization request queue in shared input mode
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The queue open operation completes successfully with no errors
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The request queue status must be marked as open and ready, enabling the program to proceed with reading authorization request messages from the queue

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark Request Queue as Open and Ready for Message Reading
all_rules.Rule_Description: Upon successfully opening the authorization request queue, the system must record the queue's availability status so that subsequent processing steps know the queue is ready for reading authorization request messages.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has attempted to open the authorization request queue in shared input mode
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The queue open operation fails for any reason
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) record the error location as 'M001', (2) classify the error as a critical MQ error, (3) capture both the completion code and the reason code as error diagnostic details, (4) set the error message to 'REQ MQ OPEN ERROR', (5) write the error log entry, and (6) immediately terminate all authorization processing since no request messages can be received

all_rules.Rule_Name: Log Critical Error and Halt Processing When Request Queue Cannot Be Opened
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the authorization request queue cannot be opened, the failure must be recorded as a critical error with full diagnostic details, and all further authorization processing must be immediately halted since no messages can be received.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The MQ request queue has been successfully opened and is ready to receive messages, and the system is configured with a wait interval of 5000 milliseconds
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system attempts to read the next available authorization request message from the MQ request queue
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system retrieves the next message from the queue into the message buffer, capturing the full message data length, and the read operation result (completion code and reason code) is available for further processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Read Next Authorization Request Message from Queue
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system attempts to retrieve the next available authorization request message from the MQ request queue using shared input mode with a configured wait interval, converting the message to the required string format.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization request message has been successfully read from the MQ request queue (read completion code indicates success)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The message is successfully retrieved
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The correlation ID from the message descriptor header of the retrieved message is saved into the working storage correlation ID field, to be used later for routing the authorization response back to the original requester

all_rules.Rule_Name: Save Correlation ID from Successfully Retrieved Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an authorization request message is successfully retrieved from the queue, the system saves the message correlation ID from the message header so that the authorization response can be matched back to the original request by the requester.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization request message has been successfully read from the MQ request queue (read completion code indicates success)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The message is successfully retrieved
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The reply-to queue name from the message descriptor header of the retrieved message is saved into the working storage reply queue name field, to be used later as the destination queue when sending the authorization response

all_rules.Rule_Name: Save Reply-To Queue Name from Successfully Retrieved Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an authorization request message is successfully retrieved from the queue, the system saves the reply-to queue name from the message header so that the authorization response is sent to the correct destination queue specified by the requester.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has attempted to read the next authorization request message from the MQ request queue
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The read attempt fails because no messages are available in the queue (the reason code indicates no message available)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The 'No More Messages Available' flag is set to TRUE, which causes the main authorization processing loop to stop iterating and no further message reads are attempted in the current execution cycle

all_rules.Rule_Name: Stop Processing Loop When No More Messages Are Available
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the system attempts to read from the MQ request queue and the queue contains no more messages, the processing loop is flagged to stop, preventing further attempts to read authorization requests in the current execution cycle.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has attempted to read the next authorization request message from the MQ request queue, and the read has failed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The read failure reason is anything other than 'no message available' (i.e., an unexpected or system-level error has occurred)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: A critical error log entry is created with: error location code 'M003', error type flagged as critical, error code 1 set to the read completion code, error code 2 set to the read reason code, error message set to 'FAILED TO READ REQUEST MQ', and the card number recorded as the event key; the program then terminates immediately after logging the error

all_rules.Rule_Name: Log Critical Error and Terminate on Unexpected Message Read Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the system encounters an unexpected failure while attempting to read an authorization request message from the queue (any failure other than no message available), a critical error is logged with full error details including the card number, and the program is terminated immediately.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization request message has arrived in the MQ Request Queue and has been read into the message buffer
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to parse the authorization request message
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The message must be recognized as a comma-delimited text string containing exactly 18 positional fields in the following fixed sequence: Authorization Date, Authorization Time, Card Number, Authorization Type, Card Expiry Date, Message Type, Message Source, Processing Code, Transaction Amount, Merchant Category Code, Acquirer Country Code, POS Entry Mode, Merchant ID, Merchant Name, Merchant City, Merchant State, Merchant ZIP Code, and Transaction ID

all_rules.Rule_Name: Authorization Request Message Format Definition
all_rules.Rule_Description: Defines the structure and format of an incoming authorization request message received from the MQ Request Queue. The message is a single text string with all fields separated by commas in a fixed positional sequence of 18 fields.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A raw authorization request message buffer has been received from the MQ Request Queue containing all authorization fields as a single comma-delimited text string
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system splits the message using the comma character as the delimiter
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All 18 fields must be extracted simultaneously in their fixed positional sequence and stored in their respective data fields: Authorization Date, Authorization Time, Card Number, Authorization Type, Card Expiry Date, Message Type, Message Source, Processing Code, Transaction Amount (as text), Merchant Category Code, Acquirer Country Code, POS Entry Mode, Merchant ID, Merchant Name, Merchant City, Merchant State, Merchant ZIP Code, and Transaction ID

all_rules.Rule_Name: Parse Authorization Request Message by Comma Delimiter
all_rules.Rule_Description: Defines the parsing mechanism for splitting the raw authorization request message into individual data fields using the comma character as the field delimiter, extracting all 18 fields simultaneously in their positional order.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A comma-delimited authorization request message has been received and is being parsed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system extracts fields from positions 1 through 3 of the message
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The following transaction identity fields must be populated from the message in positional order: Authorization Date (position 1), Authorization Time (position 2), and Card Number (position 3)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Extract Transaction Identity Fields from Authorization Request
all_rules.Rule_Description: Defines the extraction of the three core transaction identity fields from the first three positional slots of the comma-delimited authorization request message. These fields uniquely identify when and by whom the authorization was initiated.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A comma-delimited authorization request message has been received and is being parsed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system extracts fields from positions 4 through 8 of the message
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The following transaction type fields must be populated from the message in positional order: Authorization Type (position 4), Card Expiry Date (position 5), Message Type (position 6), Message Source (position 7), and Processing Code (position 8)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Extract Transaction Type Classification Fields from Authorization Request
all_rules.Rule_Description: Defines the extraction of five transaction classification and type fields from positions 4 through 8 of the comma-delimited authorization request message. These fields describe the nature, origin, and processing characteristics of the authorization request.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A comma-delimited authorization request message has been received and is being parsed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system extracts the field at position 9 of the message
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction Amount must be extracted and stored as a text string value in a temporary alphanumeric holding field, ready for subsequent numeric conversion before any financial calculations are performed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Extract Transaction Amount as Text String from Authorization Request
all_rules.Rule_Description: Defines the extraction of the Transaction Amount from position 9 of the comma-delimited authorization request message. The amount is initially extracted as a text string because it is embedded in a text-based message format and requires a subsequent conversion step before it can be used in financial calculations.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A comma-delimited authorization request message has been received and is being parsed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system extracts fields from positions 10 through 17 of the message
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The following merchant detail fields must be populated from the message in positional order: Merchant Category Code (position 10), Acquirer Country Code (position 11), POS Entry Mode (position 12), Merchant ID (position 13), Merchant Name (position 14), Merchant City (position 15), Merchant State (position 16), and Merchant ZIP Code (position 17)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Extract Merchant Details from Authorization Request
all_rules.Rule_Description: Defines the extraction of eight merchant and transaction channel fields from positions 10 through 17 of the comma-delimited authorization request message. These fields identify the merchant, their location, the country of the acquiring bank, and how the card was presented at the point of sale.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A comma-delimited authorization request message has been received and is being parsed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system extracts the field at position 18 of the message
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction ID must be extracted and stored as the unique reference identifier for this authorization request

all_rules.Rule_Name: Extract Transaction Reference ID from Authorization Request
all_rules.Rule_Description: Defines the extraction of the Transaction ID from position 18, the final positional slot of the comma-delimited authorization request message. The Transaction ID serves as the unique reference identifier for the authorization request.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Amount has been extracted from the authorization request message as a text string and stored in a temporary alphanumeric holding field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system converts the Transaction Amount for use in financial processing
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The text string Transaction Amount must be converted to a numeric value using a numeric evaluation function and stored in the numeric Transaction Amount field; the numeric value must also be copied to the working storage Transaction Amount field so it is available for all subsequent authorization decision calculations including available credit comparison

all_rules.Rule_Name: Convert Transaction Amount from Text to Numeric for Financial Processing
all_rules.Rule_Description: Defines the mandatory conversion of the Transaction Amount from its extracted text string representation into a numeric value. This conversion is required before the amount can be used in any financial calculations such as available credit comparison or approved amount assignment.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization request message has been received from the request queue as a comma-delimited text string containing 18 fields: Authorization Date, Authorization Time, Card Number, Authorization Type, Card Expiry Date, Message Type, Message Source, Processing Code, Transaction Amount, Merchant Category Code, Acquirer Country Code, POS Entry Mode, Merchant ID, Merchant Name, Merchant City, Merchant State, Merchant ZIP, and Transaction ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system parses the full request message by splitting on comma delimiters to extract each individual field into its corresponding data element
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction Amount is extracted as an alphanumeric text string into the working storage field WS-TRANSACTION-AMT-AN, representing the 9th positional field in the comma-delimited message, ready for subsequent numeric conversion

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transaction Amount Extraction from Comma-Delimited Request Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: The authorization request message arrives as a single comma-delimited text string. The transaction amount is the 9th field in this string and is extracted in alphanumeric text format as part of parsing all 18 request fields.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The transaction amount has been extracted from the comma-delimited authorization request message and is held as an alphanumeric text string in the working storage field WS-TRANSACTION-AMT-AN (e.g., the string '1234.56')
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system applies a numeric value conversion function (NUMVAL) to the alphanumeric transaction amount string
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The alphanumeric text string is converted to its equivalent numeric value (e.g., '1234.56' becomes the numeric value 1234.56) and stored in the authorization request transaction amount field PA-RQ-TRANSACTION-AMT, which is capable of supporting arithmetic operations

all_rules.Rule_Name: Alphanumeric Transaction Amount Conversion to Numeric Value
all_rules.Rule_Description: The transaction amount extracted from the request message is in alphanumeric text format (e.g., '1234.56') and must be converted to a true numeric value before it can be used in arithmetic calculations such as available credit comparison.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The transaction amount has been successfully converted from alphanumeric text format to a numeric value and is held in the authorization request field PA-RQ-TRANSACTION-AMT
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system stores the converted numeric transaction amount into the working storage amount field WS-TRANSACTION-AMT
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The numeric transaction amount is available in WS-TRANSACTION-AMT for use in the authorization decision process, specifically for comparison against the available credit amount to determine approval or decline, and for inclusion in the authorization response message

all_rules.Rule_Name: Converted Numeric Transaction Amount Stored for Authorization Decision and Response
all_rules.Rule_Description: Once the transaction amount has been converted to a numeric value, it must be stored in a working storage field that is accessible to both the authorization decision logic (available credit comparison) and the response message construction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization request has been received containing a Card Number
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system performs a lookup of the Card Number in the Card Cross-Reference (CCXREF) file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system retrieves the full Card Cross-Reference record associated with that Card Number, which contains the linked Account ID and Customer ID

all_rules.Rule_Name: Card Number Lookup in Cross-Reference File
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an authorization request is received, the card number from the request must be looked up in the Card Cross-Reference (CCXREF) file to determine whether the card is known to the system and to retrieve its linked account and customer identifiers.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A lookup of the Card Number has been performed against the Card Cross-Reference (CCXREF) file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Card Number is found in the CCXREF file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the Card Found flag to TRUE and the Card Cross-Reference record — containing the associated Account ID and Customer ID — is made available for subsequent processing steps including account record retrieval, customer record retrieval, and authorization summary retrieval

all_rules.Rule_Name: Card Found in Cross-Reference — Retrieve Account and Customer IDs
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the card number is successfully located in the Card Cross-Reference file, the system marks the card as found and makes the associated Account ID and Customer ID available for subsequent account and customer record retrieval steps.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A lookup of the Card Number has been performed against the Card Cross-Reference (CCXREF) file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Card Number is NOT found in the CCXREF file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the Card Not Found in Cross-Reference flag to TRUE, sets the Account Not Found in Master flag to TRUE, and logs a warning event with: Event Location Code = 'A001', Severity = Warning, Category = Application, Message = 'CARD NOT FOUND IN XREF', and the Card Number recorded as the event key

all_rules.Rule_Name: Card Not Found in Cross-Reference — Flag and Log Warning
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the card number submitted in the authorization request does not exist in the Card Cross-Reference file, the system must flag the card as not found, flag the account as not found, and log a business warning event identifying the card number that could not be located.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Card Cross-Reference lookup has completed and the Card Found flag has been evaluated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Card Found flag is TRUE (card was located in CCXREF with a valid Account ID and Customer ID)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system proceeds to perform all four downstream data retrieval steps in sequence: (1) Account Master Record retrieval, (2) Customer Master Record retrieval, (3) Pending Authorization Summary retrieval, and (4) Profile Data retrieval; if the Card Found flag is FALSE, all four retrieval steps are skipped

all_rules.Rule_Name: Card Found Flag Controls Downstream Data Retrieval
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Card Found flag, set during the cross-reference lookup, acts as the control gate that determines whether the system proceeds to retrieve account, customer, authorization summary, and profile data. If the card was not found, these retrieval steps are bypassed entirely.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The authorization decision has resulted in a DECLINE outcome
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The decline was caused by any of the following conditions: (1) Card Number was not found in the Card Cross-Reference file, OR (2) Account was not found in the Account Master, OR (3) Customer was not found in the Customer Master
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system assigns Authorization Response Reason Code = '3100' to the response message, indicating the card is not linked to a recognized account or customer in the system

all_rules.Rule_Name: Decline Reason Code Assignment for Card Not Found
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the authorization decision results in a decline and the root cause is that the card, account, or customer could not be found in the system, the decline reason code 3100 is assigned to the response to communicate to the requester that the card is not linked to any known account or customer.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The authorization decision has been made and the response has been sent to the requester
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Card Found in Cross-Reference flag is TRUE
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system proceeds to write the authorization results to the database, including updating or inserting the Authorization Summary record and inserting the Authorization Detail record; if the Card Found flag is FALSE, no authorization records are written to the database

all_rules.Rule_Name: Authorization Database Write Restricted to Known Cards
all_rules.Rule_Description: Authorization records — both the summary and the detail — are only written to the database when the card number was successfully found in the Card Cross-Reference file. Transactions for unknown cards do not generate any database records beyond the decline response.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A card has been successfully found in the Card Cross-Reference file, and an Account ID has been retrieved from that cross-reference record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system initiates the account record retrieval step of the authorization process
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must use the Account ID from the Card Cross-Reference record as the lookup key to read the Account Master File (ACCTDAT) and retrieve the full account record including credit limit, current balance, cash credit limit, and account status

all_rules.Rule_Name: Account Record Lookup Using Cross-Reference Account ID
all_rules.Rule_Description: When processing an authorization request, the system must use the Account ID obtained from the Card Cross-Reference file to look up the corresponding account master record in the Account Master File (ACCTDAT), which contains credit limit, current balance, cash credit limit, and account status details.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has used the Account ID from the Card Cross-Reference to look up the Account Master File (ACCTDAT)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The account record is found and successfully read from the Account Master File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must mark the account status as 'Found in Account Master' and make the following account details available for the authorization decision: Account Credit Limit, Account Current Balance, Account Cash Credit Limit, and Account Status

all_rules.Rule_Name: Successful Account Record Retrieval
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the account master record is successfully found and retrieved using the Account ID from the cross-reference, the system marks the account as found and makes the account details available for subsequent authorization decision-making, including credit limit, current balance, cash credit limit, and account status.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has used the Account ID from the Card Cross-Reference to look up the Account Master File (ACCTDAT)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: No account record is found in the Account Master File for the given Account ID
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) Mark the account status as 'Account Not Found in Master', (2) Log a business warning with the message 'ACCT NOT FOUND IN XREF' along with the Account ID as the event key, and (3) Proceed toward a decline decision for the authorization request due to missing account information

all_rules.Rule_Name: Account Record Not Found in Account Master
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the account record cannot be found in the Account Master File using the Account ID from the cross-reference, the system must mark the account as not found and log a business warning, after which the authorization process proceeds toward a decline decision due to missing account data.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has used the Account ID from the Card Cross-Reference to look up the Account Master File (ACCTDAT)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: An unexpected error occurs while reading the Account Master File — meaning the result is neither a successful read nor a record-not-found condition
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) Log a critical error with the message 'FAILED TO READ ACCT FILE', the Account ID as the event key, and the associated error response codes for diagnosis, (2) Classify the error as a critical application failure, and (3) Immediately halt all further authorization processing — no further messages are processed in the current execution cycle

all_rules.Rule_Name: Account Master File Read Failure Halts Processing
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an unexpected error occurs while attempting to read the Account Master File (other than a record not found condition), the system must log a critical error with full error details and immediately halt all further authorization processing for the current execution cycle.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A card authorization request is being processed and the Card Cross-Reference lookup has been successfully completed, yielding a Customer ID associated with the presented card number
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system initiates the customer profile retrieval step
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Customer ID from the Card Cross-Reference record must be used as the lookup key to read the Customer Master file (CUSTDAT), and the full customer profile record must be retrieved into the customer record area for use in subsequent authorization processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retrieve Customer Master Record Using Cross-Reference Customer ID
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system must use the Customer ID obtained from the Card Cross-Reference lookup to retrieve the corresponding customer profile from the Customer Master file. This establishes the link between the card presented for authorization and the customer who owns the account.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A customer record lookup has been initiated using the Customer ID obtained from the Card Cross-Reference record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Customer Master file (CUSTDAT) returns a matching record for the provided Customer ID
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must mark the customer status as 'Found in Master' (FOUND-CUST-IN-MSTR = TRUE) and continue with the authorization decision process using the retrieved customer profile information

all_rules.Rule_Name: Customer Master Record Successfully Retrieved
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Customer Master record is found in the Customer Master file using the Customer ID from the cross-reference, the system marks the customer as found and continues with the authorization process using the retrieved customer profile data.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A customer record lookup has been initiated using the Customer ID obtained from the Card Cross-Reference record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Customer Master file (CUSTDAT) does not contain a record matching the provided Customer ID
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) mark the customer status as 'Not Found in Master' (NFOUND-CUST-IN-MSTR = TRUE), (2) log a business warning event with error location code 'A003', warning severity level, application error category, error message 'CUST NOT FOUND IN XREF', and the Customer ID as the event key, and (3) continue processing — the transaction will proceed to the authorization decision step where it will be evaluated for decline

all_rules.Rule_Name: Customer Master Record Not Found — Log Warning and Continue
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Customer Master record cannot be found in the Customer Master file for the Customer ID obtained from the cross-reference, the system must flag the customer as not found, log a business warning event identifying the missing customer, and continue processing toward a decline decision rather than terminating the transaction abruptly.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The customer record lookup during authorization processing resulted in the customer not being found in the Customer Master file (NFOUND-CUST-IN-MSTR = TRUE), and the authorization decision step has determined that the transaction must be declined
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system assigns the decline reason code during the authorization decision
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The authorization response must be set to declined with response code '05', approved amount of zero, and decline reason code '3100' (indicating Card, Account, or Customer data not found in the system), and this reason code and response must be included in the authorization response message sent back to the requester

all_rules.Rule_Name: Authorization Declined Due to Customer Not Found in Master
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the customer record was not found in the Customer Master file during the authorization process, the authorization decision step must decline the transaction and assign the specific decline reason code indicating that the card, account, or customer data could not be located in the system.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A card authorization request has been received and the Card Cross-Reference record has been successfully retrieved, providing a valid Account ID linked to the card number
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to query the Pending Authorization Summary database
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Account ID obtained from the Card Cross-Reference record must be set as the search key (ACCNTID) used to query the Pending Authorization Summary segment (PAUTSUM0) in the IMS database

all_rules.Rule_Name: Use Account ID as Search Key for Pending Authorization Summary Lookup
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Account ID retrieved from the Card Cross-Reference record must be used as the unique search key to locate the Pending Authorization Summary record in the IMS database.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account ID from the Card Cross-Reference has been set as the search key
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes a Get Unique (GU) query against the IMS Pending Authorization Summary segment (PAUTSUM0) using the Account ID as the search criterion
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The IMS database returns either the matching Pending Authorization Summary record, a not-found status indicating no summary exists for the account, or an error status indicating the query could not be completed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Query IMS Database for Pending Authorization Summary Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system must perform a direct retrieval query against the IMS Pending Authorization Summary segment (PAUTSUM0) using the Account ID to determine whether an existing pending authorization summary exists for the account.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A query has been executed against the IMS Pending Authorization Summary segment (PAUTSUM0) using the Account ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The IMS database successfully locates and returns a matching Pending Authorization Summary record for the Account ID
