Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system retrieves the complete Pending Authorization Summary record containing: Credit Balance, Cash Balance, Credit Limit, Cash Credit Limit, Approved Authorization Count, Approved Authorization Amount, Declined Authorization Count, and Declined Authorization Amount — and marks the summary status as FOUND (FOUND-PAUT-SMRY-SEG) to indicate that this data is available for the available credit calculation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retrieve Pending Authorization Summary Data When Record Found
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a Pending Authorization Summary record is found in the IMS database for the account, the system retrieves all current pending authorization data including balances, limits, and authorization counts to be used in the available credit calculation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A query has been executed against the IMS Pending Authorization Summary segment (PAUTSUM0) using the Account ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The IMS database returns a segment-not-found status, indicating no Pending Authorization Summary record exists for the given Account ID
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system marks the pending authorization summary status as NOT FOUND (NFOUND-PAUT-SMRY-SEG), indicating that no existing pending authorizations exist for this account, and processing continues without raising an error or warning

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark Pending Authorization Summary as Not Found When No Record Exists
all_rules.Rule_Description: When no Pending Authorization Summary record exists in the IMS database for the account, the system marks the summary as not found, indicating this is either a new account or an account with no prior pending authorizations in the system.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Pending Authorization Summary query has completed and the summary record was NOT FOUND for the account, AND the Account Master record was successfully retrieved
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system proceeds to calculate the available credit amount for the authorization decision
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system uses the Account Master record data — specifically Account Credit Limit and Account Current Balance — as the basis for the available credit calculation, rather than the Pending Authorization Summary credit limit and credit balance

all_rules.Rule_Name: Fall Back to Account Master Data for Available Credit Calculation When Summary Not Found
all_rules.Rule_Description: When no Pending Authorization Summary record is found for the account, the available credit calculation must fall back to using the Account Master record data (Account Credit Limit and Account Current Balance) instead of the pending authorization summary data.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Pending Authorization Summary retrieval query has completed with either a FOUND or NOT FOUND result
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the result of the Pending Authorization Summary query
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system proceeds to the authorization decision step (6000-MAKE-DECISION) in both cases — if the summary was FOUND, the pending authorization summary data (Credit Limit and Credit Balance) is used for available credit calculation; if the summary was NOT FOUND, the Account Master data (Account Credit Limit and Account Current Balance) is used instead — and the authorization decision process continues without interruption

all_rules.Rule_Name: Proceed to Available Credit Calculation After Summary Retrieval Attempt
all_rules.Rule_Description: Regardless of whether the Pending Authorization Summary record was found or not found, the system must always proceed to the available credit calculation step. The outcome of the summary retrieval (found or not found) determines which data source is used for the calculation, but does not stop the authorization process.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization request has been received with a valid card number, and the card has been found in the Card Cross-Reference file with an associated Account ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system attempts to retrieve the Pending Authorization Summary record from IMS (PAUTSUM0 segment) using the Account ID
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the Pending Authorization Summary record is found, the system must use the Credit Limit and Credit Balance values from the IMS Pending Authorization Summary (PAUTSUM0) to calculate available credit. If the Pending Authorization Summary record is not found, the system must fall back to the Account Master record data for available credit calculation.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Determine Credit Data Source for Available Credit Calculation
all_rules.Rule_Description: When processing an authorization request, the system must first determine whether a Pending Authorization Summary record exists in IMS for the account, as this record takes priority over the Account Master record for available credit calculation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization request is being evaluated and the IMS Pending Authorization Summary record (PAUTSUM0) has been successfully retrieved for the account
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system calculates the available credit amount
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Available Credit Amount must be computed as: Available Credit = IMS Pending Auth Summary Credit Limit (PA-CREDIT-LIMIT) minus IMS Pending Auth Summary Credit Balance (PA-CREDIT-BALANCE). This calculated Available Credit Amount is then used to compare against the requested Transaction Amount.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Calculate Available Credit Using IMS Pending Authorization Summary Data
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the IMS Pending Authorization Summary record exists for the account, the available credit must be calculated using the Credit Limit and Credit Balance values stored in that summary record, as it reflects the most current authorization activity.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization request is being evaluated, the IMS Pending Authorization Summary record was not found for the account, and the system has previously attempted to retrieve the Account Master record from the Account Master file (ACCTDAT)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system checks whether the Account Master record was successfully retrieved
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the Account Master record was found, the system must use the Account Credit Limit and Account Current Balance from the Account Master record to calculate available credit. If the Account Master record was also not found, the system must mark the authorization for decline due to no credit data being available, without performing any credit calculation.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Determine Account Master as Fallback Credit Data Source
all_rules.Rule_Description: When no IMS Pending Authorization Summary record exists for the account, the system must determine whether the Account Master record is available as a fallback source for available credit calculation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization request is being evaluated, the IMS Pending Authorization Summary record was not found for the account, and the Account Master record has been successfully retrieved from the Account Master file (ACCTDAT)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system calculates the available credit amount using the Account Master record as the fallback data source
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Available Credit Amount must be computed as: Available Credit = Account Credit Limit (ACCT-CREDIT-LIMIT) minus Account Current Balance (ACCT-CURR-BAL). This calculated Available Credit Amount is then used to compare against the requested Transaction Amount.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Calculate Available Credit Using Account Master Record Data
all_rules.Rule_Description: When no IMS Pending Authorization Summary exists but the Account Master record is available, the available credit must be calculated using the Credit Limit and Current Balance values from the Account Master record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization request is being evaluated, the IMS Pending Authorization Summary record was not found for the account, and the Account Master record was also not found in the Account Master file (ACCTDAT)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system attempts to determine available credit for the authorization decision
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must mark the authorization decision as DECLINED. No available credit calculation is performed. The authorization proceeds to the decision outcome stage with a decline status, and no approved amount is granted.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Decline Authorization When No Credit Data is Available
all_rules.Rule_Description: When neither the IMS Pending Authorization Summary nor the Account Master record is available for the account, the authorization must be unconditionally declined as there is no credit data to evaluate the transaction against.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization request is being evaluated, and the Available Credit Amount has been successfully calculated from either the IMS Pending Authorization Summary (PA-CREDIT-LIMIT minus PA-CREDIT-BALANCE) or the Account Master record (ACCT-CREDIT-LIMIT minus ACCT-CURR-BAL)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system compares the Transaction Amount (WS-TRANSACTION-AMT) against the calculated Available Credit Amount (WS-AVAILABLE-AMT)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the Transaction Amount is greater than the Available Credit Amount, the system must mark the authorization as declined due to insufficient funds. If the Transaction Amount is less than or equal to the Available Credit Amount, the authorization has sufficient credit and may proceed toward approval.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Compare Transaction Amount Against Available Credit
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the available credit amount has been calculated from either the IMS Pending Authorization Summary or the Account Master record, the requested transaction amount must be compared against the available credit to determine if sufficient funds exist.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization request is being evaluated, the Available Credit Amount has been calculated, and the Transaction Amount (WS-TRANSACTION-AMT) is greater than the Available Credit Amount (WS-AVAILABLE-AMT)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system determines that the transaction exceeds the available credit
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must set the authorization decision to DECLINED (DECLINE-AUTH = TRUE) and set the Insufficient Funds indicator (INSUFFICIENT-FUND = TRUE). This Insufficient Funds flag will subsequently cause the authorization response reason code to be set to '4100', and the approved amount will be set to zero in the authorization response.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark Authorization as Declined Due to Insufficient Funds
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the requested transaction amount exceeds the available credit, the authorization must be declined and flagged specifically as an insufficient funds decline, which will result in decline reason code 4100 being assigned in the authorization response.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization request is being evaluated, the Available Credit Amount has been calculated from either the IMS Pending Authorization Summary or the Account Master record, and the Transaction Amount (WS-TRANSACTION-AMT) is less than or equal to the Available Credit Amount (WS-AVAILABLE-AMT)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system determines that the transaction is within the available credit limit
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must not set any decline or insufficient funds flags for the credit check. The authorization decision remains as APPROVED (the default set at the start of authorization processing), and the process proceeds to the authorization decision outcome stage where the approved amount will be set equal to the full Transaction Amount and the authorization response code will be set to '00'.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Allow Authorization to Proceed When Sufficient Credit is Available
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the requested transaction amount does not exceed the available credit, the authorization has passed the credit check and may proceed toward approval, provided no other decline conditions are present.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization request has been received and the card has been found in the Cross-Reference file with a valid Account ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system checks whether a Pending Authorization Summary record exists in IMS for the account
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If a Pending Authorization Summary record is found, the system uses the Credit Limit and Credit Balance from that summary to calculate available credit. If no Pending Authorization Summary record is found, the system falls back to using the Account Master record data.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Determine Credit Data Source for Authorization Decision
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before calculating available credit, the system determines which data source to use: the IMS Pending Authorization Summary (if it exists for the account) or the Account Master record as a fallback.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A Pending Authorization Summary record has been found in IMS for the account associated with the card being authorized
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system calculates the available credit amount
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Available Credit Amount = Credit Limit (from Pending Authorization Summary) minus Current Credit Balance (from Pending Authorization Summary)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Calculate Available Credit from Pending Authorization Summary
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a Pending Authorization Summary record exists in IMS for the account, the available credit is calculated using the credit limit and current credit balance stored in that summary record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: No Pending Authorization Summary record was found in IMS for the account
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system checks whether the Account Master record was successfully retrieved
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the Account Master record is found, the system proceeds to calculate available credit using Account Master data. If the Account Master record is not found, the authorization is declined immediately due to unavailable account data.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Determine Account Master Availability When No Pending Summary Exists
all_rules.Rule_Description: When no Pending Authorization Summary exists in IMS, the system checks whether an Account Master record was successfully retrieved to use as the fallback data source for the credit availability calculation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: No Pending Authorization Summary record was found in IMS, and the Account Master record has been successfully retrieved
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system calculates the available credit amount
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Available Credit Amount = Account Credit Limit (from Account Master) minus Account Current Balance (from Account Master)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Calculate Available Credit from Account Master Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: When no Pending Authorization Summary exists in IMS but the Account Master record is available, the available credit is calculated using the credit limit and current balance from the Account Master record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: No Pending Authorization Summary record was found in IMS AND the Account Master record was not found
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system attempts to evaluate the authorization request
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The authorization is declined unconditionally with no available credit calculation performed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Decline Authorization When No Account Data Is Available
all_rules.Rule_Description: When neither a Pending Authorization Summary nor an Account Master record is available, the authorization must be declined unconditionally as there is no basis to evaluate the credit availability.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: Available credit has been calculated using the Pending Authorization Summary data (Credit Limit minus Credit Balance)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The transaction amount is compared against the calculated available credit amount
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the transaction amount is greater than the available credit amount, the authorization is flagged as Insufficient Funds and the authorization decision is set to Declined. If the transaction amount is less than or equal to the available credit amount, the authorization proceeds toward approval.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Decline Authorization for Insufficient Funds Using Pending Summary Data
all_rules.Rule_Description: When available credit is calculated from the Pending Authorization Summary, the transaction amount is compared against the available credit. If the transaction amount exceeds the available credit, the authorization is declined for insufficient funds.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: Available credit has been calculated using the Account Master data (Account Credit Limit minus Account Current Balance)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The transaction amount is compared against the calculated available credit amount
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the transaction amount is greater than the available credit amount, the authorization is flagged as Insufficient Funds and the authorization decision is set to Declined. If the transaction amount is less than or equal to the available credit amount, the authorization proceeds toward approval.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Decline Authorization for Insufficient Funds Using Account Master Data
all_rules.Rule_Description: When available credit is calculated from the Account Master record, the transaction amount is compared against the available credit. If the transaction amount exceeds the available credit, the authorization is declined for insufficient funds.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The transaction amount does not exceed the available credit amount calculated from either the Pending Authorization Summary or the Account Master record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sets the authorization decision
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The authorization status is set to Approved, the Response Code is set to '00', and the Approved Amount is set equal to the full Transaction Amount requested

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Authorization Approval Response
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the transaction amount does not exceed the available credit, the authorization is approved with a standard approval response code and the full transaction amount is confirmed as the approved amount.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A decline condition has been triggered — either the transaction amount exceeds available credit, no account data is available, or another decline condition applies
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sets the authorization decision
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The authorization status is set to Declined, the Response Code is set to '05', and the Approved Amount is set to zero

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Authorization Decline Response
all_rules.Rule_Description: When any decline condition is triggered (insufficient funds, no account data, or other decline reasons), the authorization is declined with a standard decline response code and zero approved amount.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The authorization has been declined
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the reason for decline and determines that the card was not found in the Cross-Reference file, OR the account was not found in the Account Master, OR the customer was not found in the Customer Master
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Authorization Response Reason Code is set to '3100' indicating Card or Account Not Found

all_rules.Rule_Name: Assign Decline Reason Code for Card or Account Not Found
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an authorization is declined because the card was not found in the Cross-Reference file, or the account was not found in the Account Master, or the customer was not found in the Customer Master, the decline reason code 3100 is assigned.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The authorization has been declined
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the reason for decline and determines that the transaction amount exceeded the available credit amount
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Authorization Response Reason Code is set to '4100' indicating Insufficient Funds

all_rules.Rule_Name: Assign Decline Reason Code for Insufficient Funds
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an authorization is declined specifically because the transaction amount exceeds the available credit, the decline reason code 4100 is assigned to indicate insufficient funds.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The authorization has been declined
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the reason for decline and determines that the card is not active
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Authorization Response Reason Code is set to '4200' indicating Card Not Active

all_rules.Rule_Name: Assign Decline Reason Code for Inactive Card
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an authorization is declined because the card is not in an active status, the decline reason code 4200 is assigned.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The authorization has been declined
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the reason for decline and determines that the account is closed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Authorization Response Reason Code is set to '4300' indicating Account Closed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Assign Decline Reason Code for Closed Account
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an authorization is declined because the associated account has been closed, the decline reason code 4300 is assigned.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The authorization has been declined
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the reason for decline and determines that the card has been flagged for fraud
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Authorization Response Reason Code is set to '5100' indicating Card Fraud Detected

all_rules.Rule_Name: Assign Decline Reason Code for Card Fraud
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an authorization is declined because the card has been flagged for fraudulent activity, the decline reason code 5100 is assigned.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The authorization has been declined
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the reason for decline and determines that the merchant has been flagged for fraud
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Authorization Response Reason Code is set to '5200' indicating Merchant Fraud Detected

all_rules.Rule_Name: Assign Decline Reason Code for Merchant Fraud
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an authorization is declined because the merchant has been flagged for fraudulent activity, the decline reason code 5200 is assigned.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The authorization has been declined
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the reason for decline and the reason does not match any of the defined categories: Card/Account Not Found (3100), Insufficient Funds (4100), Card Not Active (4200), Account Closed (4300), Card Fraud (5100), or Merchant Fraud (5200)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Authorization Response Reason Code is set to '9000' indicating an Other or unspecified decline reason

all_rules.Rule_Name: Assign Decline Reason Code for Other Unspecified Decline Reasons
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an authorization is declined for a reason that does not match any of the specifically defined decline reason categories, a catch-all reason code 9000 is assigned.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The authorization decision has been finalized with a Response Code (approved '00' or declined '05'), a Reason Code (if declined), and an Approved Amount
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system builds the authorization response message
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: A comma-delimited response message is constructed containing the following fields in order: Card Number, Transaction ID, Authorization ID Code, Response Code, Authorization Response Reason Code, and Approved Amount. The Reason Code field is set to '0000' for approved transactions.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Build Authorization Response Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the authorization decision is finalized, a comma-delimited response message is constructed containing all required response fields to be returned to the requesting system.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization request has been evaluated and the authorization decision is DECLINED
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The decline reason assignment process begins
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The authorization response reason code is initialized to '0000' as the default value before any specific decline cause is evaluated

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Default Authorization Decline Reason Code
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before evaluating the specific cause of a declined authorization, a default reason code of '0000' is assigned to the authorization response. This default is overwritten only when a specific decline cause is identified.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization request has been declined and the decline reason code has been initialized to '0000'
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The card number is not found in the Card Cross-Reference file, OR the account record is not found in the Account Master file, OR the customer record is not found in the Customer Master file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The authorization response reason code is set to '3100', indicating that the decline was caused by a missing Card, Account, or Customer record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Assign Decline Reason Code 3100 for Missing Card, Account, or Customer Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an authorization is declined because the card number was not found in the Card Cross-Reference file, or the associated account record was not found in the Account Master file, or the associated customer record was not found in the Customer Master file, the decline reason code must be set to '3100' to indicate a record not found condition.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization request has been declined, the decline reason code has been initialized to '0000', and the card, account, and customer records were all found (reason code 3100 does not apply)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The decline was caused by the transaction amount exceeding the available credit limit on the account (insufficient funds flag is set)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The authorization response reason code is set to '4100', indicating that the decline was caused by insufficient available credit to cover the transaction amount

all_rules.Rule_Name: Assign Decline Reason Code 4100 for Insufficient Available Credit
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an authorization is declined because the transaction amount exceeds the available credit balance on the account, the decline reason code must be set to '4100' to indicate insufficient funds. This condition is evaluated only when the card, account, and customer records are all found.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization request has been declined, the decline reason code has been initialized to '0000', and neither a missing record condition (3100) nor an insufficient funds condition (4100) caused the decline
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The decline was caused by the card not being in an active status (card-not-active flag is set)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The authorization response reason code is set to '4200', indicating that the decline was caused by the card not being active

all_rules.Rule_Name: Assign Decline Reason Code 4200 for Inactive Card
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an authorization is declined because the card associated with the transaction is not in an active status, the decline reason code must be set to '4200'. This condition is evaluated only when neither a missing record nor an insufficient funds condition caused the decline.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization request has been declined, the decline reason code has been initialized to '0000', and none of the prior conditions (missing record 3100, insufficient funds 4100, inactive card 4200) caused the decline
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The decline was caused by the account being in a closed status (account-closed flag is set)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The authorization response reason code is set to '4300', indicating that the decline was caused by the account being closed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Assign Decline Reason Code 4300 for Closed Account
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an authorization is declined because the account associated with the card has been closed, the decline reason code must be set to '4300'. This condition is evaluated only when missing record, insufficient funds, and inactive card conditions did not cause the decline.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization request has been declined, the decline reason code has been initialized to '0000', and none of the prior conditions (missing record 3100, insufficient funds 4100, inactive card 4200, closed account 4300) caused the decline
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The decline was caused by fraud being detected on the card (card-fraud flag is set)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The authorization response reason code is set to '5100', indicating that the decline was caused by card fraud detection

all_rules.Rule_Name: Assign Decline Reason Code 5100 for Card Fraud Detection
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an authorization is declined because fraud has been detected on the card being used for the transaction, the decline reason code must be set to '5100'. This condition is evaluated only when account-level decline conditions (missing record, insufficient funds, inactive card, closed account) did not cause the decline.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization request has been declined, the decline reason code has been initialized to '0000', and none of the prior conditions (missing record 3100, insufficient funds 4100, inactive card 4200, closed account 4300, card fraud 5100) caused the decline
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The decline was caused by fraud being detected on the merchant (merchant-fraud flag is set)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The authorization response reason code is set to '5200', indicating that the decline was caused by merchant fraud detection

all_rules.Rule_Name: Assign Decline Reason Code 5200 for Merchant Fraud Detection
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an authorization is declined because fraud has been detected on the merchant where the transaction is being attempted, the decline reason code must be set to '5200'. This condition is evaluated only when card-level and account-level decline conditions did not cause the decline.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization request has been declined, the decline reason code has been initialized to '0000', and none of the specifically defined decline conditions (missing record 3100, insufficient funds 4100, inactive card 4200, closed account 4300, card fraud 5100, merchant fraud 5200) caused the decline
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The decline cause does not match any of the defined decline reason categories (falls into the 'other' condition)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The authorization response reason code is set to '9000', indicating an unclassified or unknown decline reason

all_rules.Rule_Name: Assign Decline Reason Code 9000 for Unclassified Decline Cause
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an authorization is declined but the specific cause does not match any of the defined decline reason categories (missing record, insufficient funds, inactive card, closed account, card fraud, or merchant fraud), the decline reason code must be set to '9000' as a catch-all for unclassified decline reasons.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization request has been received and a decision has been made, with the card number and transaction ID present in the request data
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The authorization response is being prepared
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The card number from the request is copied to the response card number field, and the transaction ID from the request is copied to the response transaction ID field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Copy Card Number and Transaction ID to Authorization Response
all_rules.Rule_Description: When preparing the authorization response, the card number and transaction ID from the original request are carried forward into the response fields to identify the transaction being responded to.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization request has been received containing an authorization time value
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The authorization response is being prepared
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The authorization ID code in the response is set to the authorization time value from the original request

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Authorization ID Code from Request Authorization Time
all_rules.Rule_Description: The authorization ID code in the response is derived from the authorization time provided in the original request message, serving as the unique identifier for this authorization event.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization request has been evaluated and the decision is to approve the transaction
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The authorization response fields are being populated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The response code is set to '00' indicating approval, and the approved amount is set equal to the full transaction amount from the request

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Approved Response Code and Approved Amount
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an authorization is approved, the response code is set to '00' (approved) and the approved amount is set equal to the full transaction amount requested by the merchant.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization request has been evaluated and the decision is to decline the transaction
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The authorization response fields are being populated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The response code is set to '05' indicating decline, and the approved amount is set to zero

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Declined Response Code and Zero Approved Amount
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an authorization is declined, the response code is set to '05' (declined) and the approved amount is set to zero, indicating no funds are authorized for this transaction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization decision has been made (either approved or declined)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The decline reason code field is being initialized prior to specific reason code evaluation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The decline reason code is set to '0000' as the default value

all_rules.Rule_Name: Initialize Default Decline Reason Code
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before evaluating the specific reason for a decline, the decline reason code is initialized to '0000' as a default value. This default applies to both approved and declined transactions before any specific reason code is assigned.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization transaction has been declined
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The decline was caused by the card number not being found in the card cross-reference file, OR the account not being found in the account master file, OR the customer not being found in the customer master file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The decline reason code is set to '3100' indicating that the card, account, or customer record could not be located

all_rules.Rule_Name: Assign Reason Code 3100 for Card, Account, or Customer Not Found
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a transaction is declined because the card number was not found in the card cross-reference file, or the associated account was not found in the account master, or the associated customer was not found in the customer master, the decline reason code is set to '3100'.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization transaction has been declined
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The decline was caused by the transaction amount exceeding the available credit balance on the account
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The decline reason code is set to '4100' indicating insufficient available credit

all_rules.Rule_Name: Assign Reason Code 4100 for Insufficient Available Credit
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a transaction is declined because the transaction amount exceeds the available credit on the account, the decline reason code is set to '4100' indicating insufficient funds.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization transaction has been declined
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The decline was caused by the card not being in an active status
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The decline reason code is set to '4200' indicating the card is not active

all_rules.Rule_Name: Assign Reason Code 4200 for Inactive Card
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a transaction is declined because the card associated with the request is not in an active status, the decline reason code is set to '4200' indicating the card is not active.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization transaction has been declined
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The decline was caused by the associated account being in a closed status
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The decline reason code is set to '4300' indicating the account is closed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Assign Reason Code 4300 for Closed Account
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a transaction is declined because the account associated with the card has been closed, the decline reason code is set to '4300' indicating the account is closed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization transaction has been declined
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The decline was caused by the card being flagged for fraud
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The decline reason code is set to '5100' indicating card fraud

all_rules.Rule_Name: Assign Reason Code 5100 for Card Fraud
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a transaction is declined because the card has been flagged for fraudulent activity, the decline reason code is set to '5100' indicating card fraud.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization transaction has been declined
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The decline was caused by the merchant being flagged for fraud
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The decline reason code is set to '5200' indicating merchant fraud

all_rules.Rule_Name: Assign Reason Code 5200 for Merchant Fraud
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a transaction is declined because the merchant involved in the transaction has been flagged for fraudulent activity, the decline reason code is set to '5200' indicating merchant fraud.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization transaction has been declined
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The decline reason does not match any of the defined conditions: card not found, account not found, customer not found, insufficient funds, card not active, account closed, card fraud, or merchant fraud
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The decline reason code is set to '9000' indicating an other or unknown decline reason

all_rules.Rule_Name: Assign Reason Code 9000 for Other or Unknown Decline Reason
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a transaction is declined for a reason that does not match any of the specifically defined decline conditions, the decline reason code is set to '9000' as a catch-all for other or unknown decline reasons.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization transaction has been approved with response code '00'
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The decline reason code evaluation step is reached during response preparation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The decline reason code evaluation is bypassed entirely and the reason code retains its default value of '0000', as no decline reason is applicable for an approved transaction

all_rules.Rule_Name: Approved Transactions Retain Default Reason Code with No Override
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a transaction is approved, the decline reason code evaluation is skipped entirely. The reason code remains at its default value of '0000', as no decline reason is applicable for approved transactions.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All authorization response fields have been populated including card number, transaction ID, authorization ID code, response code (either '00' for approved or '05' for declined), decline reason code, and approved amount
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The final response message is being assembled for transmission
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: A comma-delimited response message is built in the following exact sequence: (1) Card Number, (2) Transaction ID, (3) Authorization ID Code, (4) Response Code, (5) Decline Reason Code, (6) Approved Amount — with each field separated by a comma delimiter

all_rules.Rule_Name: Assemble Final Authorization Response Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: The final authorization response message is assembled as a comma-delimited string containing all required response fields in a defined sequence: card number, transaction ID, authorization ID code, response code, decline reason code, and approved amount.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization decision has been made and a reply queue name was captured from the original authorization request message
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to send the authorization response
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The response destination must be set to the reply queue name that was saved from the original request message, and the queue object type must be set to a standard queue type so the response is delivered to the correct requester

all_rules.Rule_Name: Route Authorization Response to Requester's Reply Queue
all_rules.Rule_Description: The authorization response must be routed back to the exact reply queue that was specified by the requester in the original authorization request message, ensuring the response reaches the correct destination.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has saved the Correlation ID from the original authorization request message and is preparing the response message
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The response message header is being constructed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The message type must be set to REPLY, the Correlation ID on the response must be set to the same Correlation ID that was received on the original request message, the Message ID on the response must be set to none (system-generated), and the reply-to queue and reply-to queue manager fields must be cleared to blank

all_rules.Rule_Name: Correlate Authorization Response to Original Request
all_rules.Rule_Description: The authorization response message must be explicitly linked to the original authorization request by setting the message type as a reply and carrying forward the correlation ID from the original request, enabling the requester to match the response to their specific request.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The authorization response message is being prepared for delivery
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The message delivery properties are set
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The message must be marked as non-persistent so it is not stored to disk, and the message expiry must be set to 50 units, after which the message will be automatically discarded if not consumed by the requester

all_rules.Rule_Name: Authorization Response Message Delivery Policy
all_rules.Rule_Description: Authorization response messages are transient in nature and must not be stored permanently on the queue. They must expire after a defined period to prevent stale authorization responses from being consumed by the requester.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization decision has been completed for a card transaction
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The authorization response message is constructed and placed on the reply queue
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The response message must be a comma-delimited string containing exactly the following fields in order: Card Number, Transaction ID, Authorization ID Code (set from the Authorization Time of the original request), Response Code (00 for Approved or 05 for Declined), Decline Reason Code (0000 if approved, or a specific reason code if declined), and Approved Amount (equal to the transaction amount if approved, or zero if declined)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Authorization Response Message Content Definition
all_rules.Rule_Description: The authorization response message sent back to the requester must contain a defined set of fields that fully communicate the authorization decision, enabling the requester to process the outcome of their authorization request.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The authorization response message has been fully constructed with all required fields and the reply queue destination has been configured with the correct queue name, message type, correlation ID, persistence, and expiry settings
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes the message send operation to the reply queue
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The response message must be placed onto the reply queue using a single-call put operation (MQPUT1) that opens the queue, puts the message, and closes the queue atomically, with the message send operation executed outside of any syncpoint control so the response is immediately available to the requester without waiting for a commit

all_rules.Rule_Name: Send Authorization Response to Reply Queue
all_rules.Rule_Description: The fully constructed authorization response message must be placed onto the designated MQ reply queue in a single atomic operation, delivering the authorization decision to the requester.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has attempted to send the authorization response message to the reply queue
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The send operation returns a completion code that is not successful (not equal to MQCC-OK)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must log a critical error recording the error location code as 'M004', the error category as MQ error, the completion code returned by the send operation as the first error code, the reason code returned by the send operation as the second error code, the error message 'FAILED TO PUT ON REPLY MQ', and the card number as the event key; and because the error is critical, the program must immediately terminate all processing, close the request queue, terminate the IMS PSB if scheduled, and end execution

all_rules.Rule_Name: Handle Authorization Response Send Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the authorization response cannot be successfully placed onto the reply queue, the failure must be recorded as a critical error with full diagnostic details, and the program must terminate immediately to prevent any further processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization request has been processed for a card account AND no Pending Authorization Summary record currently exists in the IMS database for that account
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to update the Authorization Summary
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: A new Pending Authorization Summary record is initialized with all numeric fields set to zero AND the Account ID is populated from the Card Cross-Reference record AND the Customer ID is populated from the Card Cross-Reference record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Initialize New Pending Authorization Summary Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: When no existing Pending Authorization Summary record is found for an account, a new summary record must be initialized with the Account ID and Customer ID sourced from the Card Cross-Reference data before any updates are applied.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization request has been processed for a card account AND the Account Master Record has been successfully retrieved
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system updates the Pending Authorization Summary record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Credit Limit in the summary record is updated with the current Credit Limit value from the Account Master Record AND the Cash Credit Limit in the summary record is updated with the current Cash Credit Limit value from the Account Master Record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Refresh Credit Limits from Account Master Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before recording any authorization activity, the Credit Limit and Cash Credit Limit values in the Pending Authorization Summary must always be refreshed with the current values from the Account Master Record, regardless of whether the summary record is new or existing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization request has been evaluated AND the authorization decision is APPROVED with an approved amount equal to the requested transaction amount
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system updates the Pending Authorization Summary record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Approved Authorization Count is incremented by 1 AND the Approved Authorization Amount Total is increased by the approved transaction amount AND the Credit Balance is increased by the approved transaction amount AND the Cash Balance is set to zero

all_rules.Rule_Name: Update Summary Counts and Balances for Approved Authorization
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an authorization is approved, the Pending Authorization Summary must reflect the new approval by incrementing the approved transaction count, adding the approved amount to the cumulative approved authorization total, increasing the credit balance by the approved amount, and resetting the cash balance to zero.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization request has been evaluated AND the authorization decision is DECLINED with an approved amount of zero
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system updates the Pending Authorization Summary record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Declined Authorization Count is incremented by 1 AND the Declined Authorization Amount Total is increased by the original requested transaction amount AND the Credit Balance remains unchanged AND the Cash Balance remains unchanged

all_rules.Rule_Name: Update Summary Counts and Amounts for Declined Authorization
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an authorization is declined, the Pending Authorization Summary must reflect the declined transaction by incrementing the declined transaction count and adding the original requested transaction amount to the cumulative declined authorization total. No changes are made to credit balance or cash balance.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Pending Authorization Summary record was successfully retrieved from the IMS database at the start of authorization processing AND all count, amount, and balance fields have been updated with the current transaction's data
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system persists the updated Pending Authorization Summary
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The existing Pending Authorization Summary record in the IMS database is replaced with the updated record containing the new counts, amounts, and balances

all_rules.Rule_Name: Persist Authorization Summary - Update Existing Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a Pending Authorization Summary record already existed in the database prior to this transaction, the updated summary data must be saved by replacing the existing record in the IMS database.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: No Pending Authorization Summary record existed in the IMS database for the account at the start of authorization processing AND a new summary record has been initialized with Account ID, Customer ID, Credit Limit, Cash Credit Limit, and the current transaction's count and amount data
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system persists the new Pending Authorization Summary
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: A new Pending Authorization Summary record is inserted into the IMS database containing the Account ID, Customer ID, refreshed credit limits, and the initial authorization counts and amounts from this transaction

all_rules.Rule_Name: Persist Authorization Summary - Insert New Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: When no Pending Authorization Summary record existed in the database prior to this transaction, the newly initialized and updated summary data must be saved by inserting a brand new record into the IMS database.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization request has been processed and an authorization detail record is about to be inserted into the database
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to record the authorization detail
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must capture the current date in YYDDD (year and day-of-year) format, the current time in HHMMSS format, and the current milliseconds, then combine the time and milliseconds into a single time-with-milliseconds value by multiplying the time by 1000 and adding the milliseconds, so that the authorization event is timestamped with full precision

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture Current Timestamp with Millisecond Precision for Authorization Detail
all_rules.Rule_Description: When inserting an authorization detail record, the system must capture the exact current date and time including milliseconds to provide a precise timestamp for the authorization event.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The current date has been captured in YYDDD format as a 5-digit value and the current time with milliseconds has been computed as a 9-digit value
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the authorization detail record for insertion
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must compute the Date Sort Key as 99999 minus the current YYDDD date value, and compute the Time Sort Key as 999999999 minus the current time-with-milliseconds value, so that when authorization records are retrieved in ascending sort key order, the most recently created records are returned first

all_rules.Rule_Name: Compute Reverse Chronological Sort Keys for Authorization History Retrieval
all_rules.Rule_Description: To ensure that the most recent authorization records appear first when retrieving authorization history, the system computes complement-based sort keys by subtracting the current date and time from their maximum values.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization request message has been successfully parsed and the authorization decision has been made
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the authorization detail record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must copy the following fields from the original authorization request to the detail record: Authorization Original Date, Authorization Original Time, Card Number, Authorization Type, Card Expiry Date, Message Type, Message Source, Processing Code, Transaction Amount, and Transaction ID — preserving all original request values exactly as received

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Transaction Details on Authorization Detail Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: All core transaction details from the original authorization request must be captured and stored on the authorization detail record to provide a complete audit trail of the transaction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization request message has been successfully parsed and the authorization decision has been made
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the authorization detail record with merchant information
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must copy the following fields from the original authorization request to the detail record: Merchant Category Code, Acquirer Country Code, POS Entry Mode, Merchant ID, Merchant Name, Merchant City, Merchant State, and Merchant ZIP — preserving all original merchant values exactly as received

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Merchant Details on Authorization Detail Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: All merchant-related details from the original authorization request must be captured and stored on the authorization detail record to support merchant-level reporting and fraud analysis.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization decision has been made and the response has been prepared
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the authorization detail record with response information
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must copy the following fields from the authorization response to the detail record: Authorization ID Code (the time of authorization used as the auth identifier), Authorization Response Code (00 for Approved or 05 for Declined), Authorization Response Reason Code (3100=Card/Account/Customer Not Found, 4100=Insufficient Funds, 4200=Card Not Active, 4300=Account Closed, 5100=Card Fraud, 5200=Merchant Fraud, 9000=Other), and Approved Amount (equal to the transaction amount if approved, or zero if declined)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Authorization Response Details on Authorization Detail Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: The authorization response details including the decision outcome, reason code, and approved amount must be stored on the authorization detail record to provide a complete record of the authorization result.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization request has been evaluated and the decision is Approved
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sets the status on the authorization detail record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The authorization detail record status must be set to PENDING MATCH, indicating that the approved transaction is awaiting a corresponding settlement transaction to be matched against it

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Authorization Detail Status to Pending Match When Transaction is Approved
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an authorization is approved, the authorization detail record must be flagged with a status of Pending Match to indicate that the transaction has been authorized but is awaiting settlement matching.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization request has been evaluated and the decision is Declined
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sets the status on the authorization detail record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The authorization detail record status must be set to AUTH DECLINED, indicating that the transaction was rejected and will not be matched against any settlement transaction

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Authorization Detail Status to Auth Declined When Transaction is Declined
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an authorization is declined, the authorization detail record must be flagged with a status of Auth Declined to indicate that the transaction was rejected and will not proceed to settlement.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization detail record is being prepared for insertion, regardless of whether the transaction was approved or declined
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system initializes the fraud-related fields on the authorization detail record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Fraud Flag field must be set to blank (space) and the Fraud Report Date field must be set to blank (space), indicating that no fraud has been identified or reported at the time of authorization

all_rules.Rule_Name: Initialize Fraud Indicators to Blank on New Authorization Detail Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: At the time of authorization, no fraud has been identified or reported, so the fraud-related fields on the authorization detail record must be initialized to blank to reflect a clean fraud status at the point of authorization.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The card number has been successfully found in the Card Cross-Reference file and the associated Account ID has been retrieved
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to insert the authorization detail record into the database
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Account ID from the Card Cross-Reference record must be assigned to the authorization detail record's Account ID field, establishing the parent-child relationship between the account and the authorization detail

all_rules.Rule_Name: Link Authorization Detail Record to Account via Card Cross-Reference
all_rules.Rule_Description: The authorization detail record must be linked to the correct account by assigning the Account ID obtained from the Card Cross-Reference lookup, ensuring the detail record is associated with the correct account owner.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The authorization detail record has been fully populated with transaction details, merchant details, response details, status, fraud indicators, and account linkage
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system inserts the authorization detail record into the IMS database
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must insert the authorization detail record as a child segment under the parent account authorization summary segment, navigating to the correct parent using the Account ID; if the insert is successful, processing continues normally; if the insert fails, a critical error must be logged identifying the card number associated with the failed insert and the IMS error code, and the program must immediately stop processing and terminate

all_rules.Rule_Name: Insert Authorization Detail Record as Child Segment Under Account Summary in IMS Database
all_rules.Rule_Description: The fully populated authorization detail record must be inserted into the IMS database as a child segment under the parent account authorization summary segment, linked by Account ID. If the insert fails, a critical error must be logged and processing must stop.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization transaction has been evaluated and a detail record is being prepared for insertion into the authorization database
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system is ready to record the timestamp for the authorization detail record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must capture the current system date and time with millisecond precision as the authoritative timestamp for the authorization event, producing an absolute time value that serves as the basis for all subsequent date, time, and sort key derivations

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture Current System Timestamp with Millisecond Precision for Authorization Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: When inserting a new authorization detail record, the system must capture the exact current date and time including milliseconds to precisely timestamp the authorization event.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The current system timestamp has been captured with millisecond precision
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system formats the captured timestamp to extract the date component
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must extract the date in YYDDD format (2-digit year + 3-digit day-of-year) and store the first 5 characters as the working date value (WS-YYDDD) to be used in the reverse date sort key computation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Extract Authorization Date in Year and Day-of-Year Format (YYDDD)
all_rules.Rule_Description: The current date must be extracted from the captured timestamp in YYDDD format (2-digit year followed by 3-digit day-of-year) to serve as the basis for computing the reverse chronological date sort key on the authorization detail record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The current system timestamp has been captured with millisecond precision
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system formats the captured timestamp to extract the time component
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must extract the time in HHMMSS format and store it as a numeric value (WS-CUR-TIME-N6) to be used in the combined time-with-milliseconds calculation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Extract Authorization Time in HHMMSS Format
all_rules.Rule_Description: The current time must be extracted from the captured timestamp in HHMMSS format (hours, minutes, seconds) to serve as the base time value for combining with milliseconds and computing the reverse chronological time sort key.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The current system timestamp has been captured with millisecond precision
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system formats the captured timestamp to extract its components
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must extract the milliseconds component (WS-CUR-TIME-MS) as a separate value from the timestamp, distinct from the HHMMSS time value, so that it can be combined with the time value to achieve millisecond-level precision in the sort key

all_rules.Rule_Name: Extract Milliseconds Component from Current Timestamp
all_rules.Rule_Description: The milliseconds component must be separately extracted from the captured timestamp to enable millisecond-precision time stamping and to form the 9-digit combined time value used in the reverse chronological sort key.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The current time has been extracted in HHMMSS numeric format (WS-CUR-TIME-N6) and the milliseconds component (WS-CUR-TIME-MS) has been separately extracted from the system timestamp
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system computes the combined precision time value
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must calculate the combined time value as: Combined Time Value (WS-TIME-WITH-MS) = (HHMMSS Time Value × 1000) + Milliseconds, producing a single 9-digit numeric value that represents the time with millisecond precision

all_rules.Rule_Name: Combine Time and Milliseconds into 9-Digit Precision Time Value
all_rules.Rule_Description: The HHMMSS time value and the milliseconds component must be mathematically combined into a single 9-digit numeric value to represent time with millisecond precision, which is then used to compute the reverse chronological time sort key.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The current date has been extracted in YYDDD format and stored as a 5-digit numeric value (WS-YYDDD)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system computes the reverse date sort key for the authorization detail record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must calculate the Reverse Date Sort Key (PA-AUTH-DATE-9C) as: 99999 minus the current YYDDD date value, ensuring that a later date produces a smaller sort key value so that the most recent authorization records sort first when retrieved from the database

all_rules.Rule_Name: Compute Reverse Chronological Date Sort Key for Authorization Detail Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: A reverse date sort key must be computed by subtracting the current YYDDD date from the maximum value of 99999, so that the most recent authorization records appear first when the authorization history is retrieved in chronological order.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The combined time value with millisecond precision (WS-TIME-WITH-MS) has been computed as a 9-digit numeric value
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system computes the reverse time sort key for the authorization detail record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must calculate the Reverse Time Sort Key (PA-AUTH-TIME-9C) as: 999999999 minus the Combined Time Value (WS-TIME-WITH-MS), ensuring that a later time produces a smaller sort key value so that the most recent authorization records within the same date sort first when retrieved from the database

all_rules.Rule_Name: Compute Reverse Chronological Time Sort Key for Authorization Detail Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: A reverse time sort key must be computed by subtracting the 9-digit combined time value (time with milliseconds) from the maximum value of 999999999, so that the most recent authorization records within the same date appear first when authorization history is retrieved.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The reverse date sort key (PA-AUTH-DATE-9C) has been computed as 99999 minus the current YYDDD date, and the reverse time sort key (PA-AUTH-TIME-9C) has been computed as 999999999 minus the combined time-with-milliseconds value
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The authorization detail record is being prepared for insertion into the authorization database
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Both the reverse date sort key (PA-AUTH-DATE-9C) and the reverse time sort key (PA-AUTH-TIME-9C) must be stored as fields on the authorization detail record (PENDING-AUTH-DETAILS), so that when authorization history is queried, records are returned in reverse chronological order with the most recent authorization appearing first, ordered first by date and then by time within the same date

all_rules.Rule_Name: Store Reverse Chronological Sort Keys on Authorization Detail Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: Both the reverse date sort key and the reverse time sort key must be stored as fields on the authorization detail record in the database, enabling the authorization history to be retrieved in reverse chronological order with the most recent transactions appearing first.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The authorization processing program has been initialized, the request message queue has been opened, and the first authorization request message has been read from the queue
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The message processing loop evaluates its continuation conditions at the start of each iteration
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The loop continues processing authorization requests if and only if both conditions are false: (1) the 'No More Messages Available' flag is NOT set, AND (2) the 'Loop End' flag is NOT set. If either flag is set to true, the loop exits and no further authorization messages are processed in this execution cycle

all_rules.Rule_Name: Authorization Request Message Processing Loop Execution Control
all_rules.Rule_Description: Controls the continuous processing loop that iterates over incoming authorization request messages. The loop continues as long as messages are available in the queue and the processing limit has not been reached.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A raw authorization request message has been successfully retrieved from the request queue and is available in the message buffer
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system parses the comma-delimited message content
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The following 18 fields are extracted in sequence from the message: Authorization Date, Authorization Time, Card Number, Authorization Type, Card Expiry Date, Message Type, Message Source, Processing Code, Transaction Amount (alphanumeric), Merchant Category Code, Acquirer Country Code, POS Entry Mode, Merchant ID, Merchant Name, Merchant City, Merchant State, Merchant ZIP Code, and Transaction ID. Additionally, the Transaction Amount is converted from its alphanumeric text representation to a numeric value and stored as the official Transaction Amount for use in all subsequent calculations

all_rules.Rule_Name: Authorization Request Message Field Extraction and Parsing
all_rules.Rule_Description: Parses an incoming comma-delimited authorization request message and extracts all individual transaction data fields required for authorization processing. The transaction amount is converted from text format to a numeric value for calculation purposes.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization request message has been successfully parsed and all transaction fields have been extracted
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system is ready to evaluate and respond to the authorization request
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The full authorization processing module is invoked, which performs: card cross-reference lookup, account master lookup, customer master lookup, pending authorization summary lookup, authorization decision (approve or decline), response message construction and dispatch, and database write of authorization results

all_rules.Rule_Name: Invoke Full Authorization Processing for Each Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: Triggers the complete end-to-end authorization processing workflow for each parsed authorization request message, encompassing card and account lookups, authorization decision-making, response generation, and database updates.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization request message has been fully processed including decision, response, and database updates
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The processing of a single authorization message is complete
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The messages-processed counter is incremented by exactly 1, reflecting the cumulative count of authorization messages handled in the current execution cycle

all_rules.Rule_Name: Authorization Message Processed Counter Increment
all_rules.Rule_Description: Tracks the total number of authorization request messages processed in the current execution cycle by incrementing a running counter after each message is fully processed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A single authorization request has been fully processed, including the authorization decision, response sent to the requester, and all database updates (authorization summary and authorization detail records)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system issues a commit after completing all processing for that authorization message
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All database changes associated with that single authorization transaction are permanently committed as one complete unit of work. Each authorization message is committed independently, so a failure on a subsequent message does not roll back previously committed authorizations

all_rules.Rule_Name: Commit Authorization Transaction Updates After Each Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: Ensures that all database changes resulting from processing a single authorization request are permanently committed as an independent unit of work, guaranteeing data consistency and preventing partial updates.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The database commit (syncpoint) for the current authorization message has been successfully issued
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to process the next authorization message
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The IMS database session scheduled flag is reset to 'Not Scheduled', ensuring that the next authorization transaction will establish a fresh IMS database session rather than reusing the session from the previous transaction

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reset IMS Database Session After Each Authorization Commit
all_rules.Rule_Description: After committing the database updates for a processed authorization, the IMS database session state is reset so that the next authorization message starts with a clean database session context.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The messages-processed counter has been incremented after completing an authorization message, and the IMS session has been reset
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system checks whether the number of messages processed in the current execution cycle exceeds the maximum processing limit of 500
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the messages-processed counter is greater than 500, the Loop End flag is set to true, which will cause the processing loop to exit at its next iteration check and no further authorization messages will be processed in this execution cycle. If the messages-processed counter is 500 or fewer, the Loop End flag remains unchanged and the system proceeds to read the next authorization message from the queue

all_rules.Rule_Name: Maximum Authorization Messages Per Execution Cycle Limit Enforcement
all_rules.Rule_Description: Enforces a processing cap of 500 authorization messages per execution cycle. Once the limit is reached, no further messages are processed in the current cycle, preventing runaway processing and ensuring controlled resource usage.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The messages-processed count is within the allowed limit and the processing loop is continuing, and the request message queue is open
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system attempts to retrieve the next authorization request message from the queue, waiting up to 5000 milliseconds for a message to arrive
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If a message is successfully retrieved: the message correlation identifier is saved for use in the response, and the reply queue name is captured to know where to send the authorization response. If no message is available in the queue within the wait period: the 'No More Messages Available' flag is set to true, which will cause the processing loop to exit at its next iteration check. If the message retrieval fails for any reason other than no message being available: the failure is logged as a critical error against the card number involved and the program terminates immediately

all_rules.Rule_Name: Read Next Authorization Request Message from Queue
all_rules.Rule_Description: Retrieves the next pending authorization request message from the request queue when the processing limit has not been reached. Captures the reply queue destination and message correlation identifier for use in sending the authorization response.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization request has been fully processed, including the authorization decision, response sent to the reply queue, and all database updates completed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system completes processing of the current authorization request
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The total count of processed authorization messages is incremented by 1 to reflect the completion of the current authorization

all_rules.Rule_Name: Track Number of Authorization Requests Processed
all_rules.Rule_Description: After each authorization request is fully processed (decision made, response sent, and database updated), the system increments a running count of processed authorization messages to track progress against the processing limit for the current execution cycle.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization request has been fully processed with all associated database updates pending (authorization summary updated or inserted, authorization detail record inserted) and the response has been sent to the reply queue
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system issues a syncpoint commit after completing the authorization processing
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All pending database updates for the current authorization — including the authorization summary record (updated or newly created) and the authorization detail record — are permanently committed and made durable; the system is ready to process the next authorization request independently

all_rules.Rule_Name: Commit Authorization Updates After Each Transaction
all_rules.Rule_Description: After each individual authorization request is fully processed, all pending database changes (authorization summary updates and authorization detail inserts) are permanently committed as a single unit of work, ensuring data consistency and integrity for that authorization.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The syncpoint commit has been successfully issued for the current authorization request
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system resets the IMS database session state
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The IMS database session is marked as 'not scheduled', clearing any residual session state from the completed authorization so that the next authorization request will establish a new, clean IMS database session

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reset Database Session After Each Authorization Commit
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the syncpoint commit is issued for the current authorization, the IMS database session state is reset to 'not scheduled', ensuring that the next authorization request starts with a fresh database session and does not carry over any state from the previous authorization.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has completed processing an authorization request and the processed message counter has been incremented
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates whether the total number of processed authorization messages exceeds the configured processing limit (WS-REQSTS-PROCESS-LIMIT)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the number of processed messages is greater than the processing limit, the system sets the loop-end flag to stop the processing loop and proceeds to the termination phase without reading any further authorization requests from the queue

all_rules.Rule_Name: Enforce Maximum Authorization Processing Limit Per Execution Cycle
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system enforces a maximum limit on the number of authorization requests that can be processed within a single execution cycle. Once the count of processed messages exceeds the configured processing limit, the system stops reading new authorization requests and proceeds to termination, preventing unbounded processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has completed processing an authorization request and the processed message counter has been incremented
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The count of processed authorization messages is greater than the configured processing limit (WS-REQSTS-PROCESS-LIMIT)
