Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the loop-end indicator to true, which causes the main processing loop to exit after the current iteration, and the program proceeds to the termination phase to close all open resources without processing any additional authorization requests

all_rules.Rule_Name: Stop Authorization Processing When Limit Is Reached
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the number of processed authorization messages exceeds the configured maximum processing limit for the current execution cycle, the system halts further authorization processing and signals the main processing loop to exit, proceeding to the termination phase.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has completed processing an authorization request and the processed message counter has been incremented
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The count of processed authorization messages is less than or equal to the configured processing limit (WS-REQSTS-PROCESS-LIMIT)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system reads the next authorization request message from the request MQ queue, waiting up to the configured wait interval (5000 milliseconds) for a message to arrive; if a message is available, the processing loop continues with the next authorization request; if no message is available, the loop exits and the program proceeds to termination

all_rules.Rule_Name: Continue Processing Next Authorization Request When Limit Not Reached
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the number of processed authorization messages has not yet reached the configured maximum processing limit, the system proceeds to read the next available authorization request from the request queue to continue the processing cycle.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization request is ready to be processed and IMS database access is required to retrieve account, customer, and authorization summary data
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system initiates the IMS database access session by scheduling the designated Program Specification Block (PSB)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The IMS database access session is requested and the resulting scheduling status is captured for evaluation in subsequent steps

all_rules.Rule_Name: Request IMS Database Access Session
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before processing each authorization request, the program must request access to the IMS database by scheduling the Program Specification Block (PSB). This is the first step in enabling IMS database read and write operations for the authorization cycle.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An IMS database access session has been requested for authorization processing
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The scheduling status indicates that the PSB was already active (scheduled more than once)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system identifies that an existing IMS session is already open and must be closed before proceeding with a fresh session

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Already Active IMS Database Session
all_rules.Rule_Description: After requesting an IMS database access session, the system must check whether a session was already active from a previous processing cycle. If the PSB was already scheduled more than once, the existing session must be closed before a new one is established to avoid conflicts.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The IMS database access session scheduling check reveals that a PSB session is already active from a prior processing cycle
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system detects the already-active session condition
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The existing IMS database session is terminated (closed) to release the prior session before a new session is requested

all_rules.Rule_Name: Close Existing IMS Database Session Before Rescheduling
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an IMS database session is found to be already active, the system must terminate the existing session before requesting a new one. This ensures a clean state for the new authorization processing cycle.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An existing IMS database session has been successfully terminated because it was already active
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system requests a new IMS database access session by rescheduling the Program Specification Block (PSB)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: A fresh IMS database access session is requested and the new scheduling status is captured to determine whether the session was successfully established

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reschedule IMS Database Access After Session Termination
all_rules.Rule_Description: After closing an already-active IMS session, the system must immediately request a new IMS database access session to enable processing of the current authorization request. The new scheduling status is captured for success evaluation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An IMS database access session has been requested (either as a first-time schedule or after terminating an existing session)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The scheduling status indicates success
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The IMS database session is flagged as active and ready, enabling the authorization process to proceed with reading account, customer, and authorization summary data from the IMS database

all_rules.Rule_Name: Enable IMS Database Access on Successful Scheduling
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the IMS PSB scheduling completes successfully (whether on the first attempt or after rescheduling), the system marks the IMS database session as active and ready, allowing subsequent authorization processing steps to read and write IMS database records.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An IMS database access session has been requested (either initially or after terminating an existing session)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The scheduling status indicates failure (status is not successful)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system logs a critical error with error location 'I001', error category set to IMS error, the IMS return status code captured as the error code, and the error message 'IMS SCHD FAILED'; the program then terminates immediately without processing any authorization requests

all_rules.Rule_Name: Log IMS Scheduling Failure and Terminate Processing
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the IMS PSB scheduling fails (on either the initial attempt or the rescheduling attempt after session termination), the failure is logged as a critical error with the IMS return status, error location code 'I001', and the message 'IMS SCHD FAILED'. Because this is a critical error, the program terminates immediately and cannot process any authorization requests.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The authorization processing loop is actively processing messages from the request queue
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Either no more authorization request messages are available in the request queue, OR the count of messages processed in the current execution cycle exceeds the maximum configured processing limit
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The processing loop is exited and the program termination sequence is initiated, stopping any further authorization request processing for the current execution cycle

all_rules.Rule_Name: Initiate Program Termination When Processing Limit Is Reached
all_rules.Rule_Description: The program terminates its main processing loop and initiates the termination sequence when either no more authorization request messages are available in the queue, or the number of messages processed in the current execution cycle has exceeded the configured processing limit.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program termination sequence has been initiated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The IMS PSB session is found to be currently active (scheduled)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The IMS PSB session is formally terminated, releasing all IMS database access held by the program; if no IMS PSB session is active, this step is skipped and the program proceeds directly to closing the MQ request queue

all_rules.Rule_Name: Terminate Active IMS Database Session Before Program Exit
all_rules.Rule_Description: During program termination, the system checks whether an IMS database session (PSB) is currently active. If an active session exists, it must be formally terminated to release IMS database access before the program exits.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program termination sequence has been initiated and the IMS PSB session has been handled
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The MQ request queue is found to be currently open
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The MQ request queue is formally closed to release the queue connection; if the queue is already closed, this step is skipped and the program proceeds to termination complete

all_rules.Rule_Name: Close MQ Request Queue If Currently Open During Termination
all_rules.Rule_Description: During program termination, the system checks whether the MQ request queue is currently open. If the queue is open, it must be formally closed to release the queue connection. If the queue is already closed, no action is taken and termination completes.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A request to close the MQ request queue has been submitted during program termination
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The MQ queue close operation completes successfully
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The MQ request queue is marked as closed and the program proceeds to termination complete with all resources released

all_rules.Rule_Name: Confirm Successful Closure of MQ Request Queue
all_rules.Rule_Description: After attempting to close the MQ request queue, the system verifies whether the closure was successful. A successful closure marks the queue connection as released and allows termination to complete normally.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A request to close the MQ request queue has been submitted during program termination
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The MQ queue close operation fails (completion code is not successful)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: A warning-level error is logged with error location code 'M005', the completion code, the reason code, and the message 'FAILED TO CLOSE REQUEST MQ'; the failure is classified as a non-critical MQ warning and program termination continues normally to completion without aborting

all_rules.Rule_Name: Log Non-Critical Warning When MQ Request Queue Fails to Close
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the MQ request queue cannot be closed during program termination, a warning is logged with the failure details. This is treated as a non-critical condition, meaning the program termination continues to completion rather than aborting.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The authorization processing cycle has completed and the system is in the termination phase
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system checks the current status of the MQ request queue connection
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the request queue is currently open, the system proceeds to close it; if the request queue was never opened or is already closed, the system takes no action and ends the close process

all_rules.Rule_Name: Check If Request Queue Is Open Before Closing
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before attempting to close the MQ request queue, the system verifies whether the queue was successfully opened during this processing cycle. If the queue was never opened or is already closed, no close action is taken.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The MQ request queue is currently open and the authorization processing cycle has completed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system attempts to close the MQ request queue connection
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system executes the queue close operation against the request queue connection and captures the completion code and reason code from the close operation to determine success or failure

all_rules.Rule_Name: Close MQ Request Queue Connection
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the request queue is confirmed to be open, the system initiates the closure of the MQ request queue connection to release the queue resource after all authorization messages have been processed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has attempted to close the MQ request queue connection
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The close operation completes successfully with no errors
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system marks the request queue status as closed, indicating the queue connection has been properly released

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark Request Queue as Closed on Successful Close
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the MQ request queue is successfully closed, the system updates the queue status to reflect that the queue is now closed, ensuring accurate tracking of the queue connection state.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has attempted to close the MQ request queue connection and the close operation has failed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The close operation returns an unsuccessful completion code
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system logs a warning-level error (non-critical) with error location code 'M005', the completion code from the failed close operation as the primary error code, the reason code from the failed close operation as the secondary error code, and the error message 'FAILED TO CLOSE REQUEST MQ'; processing continues to program end without termination since all authorization transactions have already been processed and committed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Log Warning When Request Queue Close Fails
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the attempt to close the MQ request queue fails, the system logs a non-critical warning with the error details. This is treated as a warning rather than a critical error, meaning the program continues to its end without aborting, as all authorization processing has already been completed and committed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An error or warning event has been detected during authorization processing (e.g., queue open failure, file read failure, IMS failure, or a business data warning such as card not found)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The error logging process is initiated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system captures the current date in YYMMDD format and the current time, which will be used as the timestamp on the error log record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture Error Timestamp for Log Entry
all_rules.Rule_Description: When any error or warning event is detected, the system must capture the current date and time to accurately timestamp the error log entry before recording it.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The current date and time have been captured for the error log entry
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The error log record is being assembled
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The error log record is populated with: the current CICS Transaction ID recorded as the Application identifier, the Authorization Program name recorded as the Program identifier, the captured current date recorded as the Error Date, and the captured current time recorded as the Error Time

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Error Log Record with Transaction and Program Identity
all_rules.Rule_Description: Each error log entry must be stamped with the identity of the transaction and program that encountered the error, enabling traceability back to the originating process.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An error or warning event has been detected and the log record identity fields have been populated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The error details are added to the log record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The error log record must include all of the following: an Error Location Code identifying the specific point in processing where the error occurred (e.g., 'M001' for MQ queue open failure, 'M003' for MQ read failure, 'M004' for MQ reply send failure, 'C001'/'C002'/'C003' for file read failures on XREF/Account/Customer files, 'A001' for card not found in cross-reference, 'A002' for account not found, 'A003' for customer not found, 'I001' for IMS PSB schedule failure, 'I002' for IMS authorization summary read failure, 'I003' for IMS authorization summary update failure, 'I004' for IMS authorization detail insert failure); an Error Severity classification of either Critical or Warning; an Error Type classification identifying the system component involved (MQ messaging system, CICS file system, IMS database, or Application business data); a primary Error Code (Error Code 1) containing the system completion code where applicable; a secondary Error Code (Error Code 2) containing the system reason code where applicable; a descriptive Error Message in plain text describing the nature of the failure (e.g., 'REQ MQ OPEN ERROR', 'FAILED TO READ REQUEST MQ', 'FAILED TO PUT ON REPLY MQ', 'FAILED TO READ XREF FILE', 'FAILED TO READ ACCT FILE', 'FAILED TO READ CUST FILE', 'IMS SCHD FAILED', 'IMS GET SUMMARY FAILED', 'IMS UPDATE SUMRY FAILED', 'IMS INSERT DETL FAILED', 'CARD NOT FOUND IN XREF', 'ACCT NOT FOUND IN XREF', 'CUST NOT FOUND IN XREF'); and the Affected Event Key identifying the business entity being processed at the time of the error, such as the Card Number or Account ID

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Error Log Record with Error Details and Affected Business Entity
all_rules.Rule_Description: Each error log entry must contain sufficient detail to identify where the error occurred, what the error was, and which business entity (e.g., card number or account ID) was being processed at the time, enabling business and operations teams to investigate and resolve issues.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The error log record has been fully populated with timestamp, transaction identity, program identity, error location code, error severity, error type, error codes, descriptive message, and affected business entity key
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The error log record is ready to be persisted
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The complete error log record is written to the System Error Log Queue named 'CSSL', and the full length of the error log record is written ensuring no data is truncated

all_rules.Rule_Name: Write Error Log Record to System Error Log Queue
all_rules.Rule_Description: Once the error log record is fully assembled with all required details, it must be written to the centralized system error log queue (CSSL) to ensure the error is permanently recorded for operational monitoring and audit purposes.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The error log record has been successfully written to the System Error Log Queue
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The error severity is evaluated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the error was classified as Critical (ERR-CRITICAL flag is set), the system must immediately initiate program termination by releasing all open resources and ending the program; if the error was classified as Warning only (ERR-CRITICAL flag is not set), the system continues processing with the next step without interruption

all_rules.Rule_Name: Classify Error Severity as Critical or Warning
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the error log record has been written, the system must evaluate the severity of the error to determine whether processing can safely continue or must be immediately terminated. This classification drives the subsequent processing path.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An error event has been detected, logged to the System Error Log Queue, and evaluated as a Warning severity (not Critical)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The severity check determines the error is Warning only
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program resumes normal processing flow from the point after the error logging call, allowing the authorization decision and response steps to proceed; the warning conditions that trigger this path include: card number not found in the Card Cross-Reference file (location A001), account not found in the Account Master file (location A002), and customer not found in the Customer Master file (location A003)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Continue Processing After Warning Event
all_rules.Rule_Description: Warning-level events represent non-fatal business data conditions (such as a card not found in the cross-reference, an account not found, or a customer not found) that are logged for visibility but do not prevent the authorization decision process from continuing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A critical error has been detected and logged, and the severity check has determined that the program must terminate
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program termination sequence is initiated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The following resource cleanup steps are performed in order: first, if an IMS PSB (Program Specification Block) database session was successfully scheduled and is currently active, it is formally terminated to release the IMS database session; second, if the Request MQ Queue was successfully opened and is currently open, it is formally closed to release the MQ queue connection; after all open resources have been released, the program ends immediately and returns control to the calling system, with no further authorization messages processed in the current execution cycle

all_rules.Rule_Name: Terminate All Open Resources on Critical Error
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a critical error is encountered, the program must safely release all open system resources — including the IMS database session and the MQ message queue connection — before ending, to prevent resource leaks and ensure system integrity.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An error condition has been detected during authorization processing, and the error record has been populated with: error location code (e.g., 'A001', 'C001', 'M001', 'I001', etc.), error type (Critical or Warning), error category (Application, CICS, MQ, or IMS), one or two error codes, an error message description, and optionally an event key (e.g., card number or account ID)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The error logging routine is invoked
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) capture the current date (in YYMMDD format) and current time, (2) record the application transaction ID as the application identifier, (3) record the program name, (4) populate the error log record with the current date and time, (5) write the complete error log record — containing application ID, program name, date, time, error location, error type, error category, error codes, error message, and event key — to the error log destination

all_rules.Rule_Name: Log Error Event with Full Audit Details
all_rules.Rule_Description: When any error condition is detected during authorization processing, the system must capture and record a complete error event including the current date and time, the application transaction identifier, the program name, the error location code, error codes, and a descriptive error message to the error log.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An error event has been logged with a severity classification of either Critical or Warning
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The error severity is evaluated after the error log has been written
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the error is classified as a Warning, processing continues normally with no interruption; if the error is classified as Critical, the system immediately invokes the termination sequence to release all active resources and end program execution

all_rules.Rule_Name: Classify Error Severity and Route Processing
all_rules.Rule_Description: After logging an error event, the system must evaluate the severity of the error to determine whether processing can continue or must be immediately terminated. Warning-level errors allow processing to continue, while critical errors trigger an immediate termination sequence.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A critical error has been detected and logged during authorization processing
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The critical error termination sequence is triggered
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must execute the full resource cleanup routine (closing IMS PSB and MQ connections as applicable) and then end program execution

all_rules.Rule_Name: Initiate Full Resource Cleanup on Critical Error
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a critical error is detected, the system must initiate a controlled termination sequence that ensures all active resources — including IMS database sessions and MQ message queue connections — are properly released before the program ends.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The termination sequence has been initiated, either due to a critical error or normal end of processing
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system checks whether an IMS PSB session is currently scheduled and active
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the IMS PSB session is active, the system must issue a formal IMS TERM command to release all IMS database resources and connections; if the IMS PSB session is not active, this step is skipped and processing continues to the next cleanup step

all_rules.Rule_Name: Terminate Active IMS Database Session on Shutdown
all_rules.Rule_Description: During the termination sequence, the system must check whether an IMS Program Specification Block (PSB) session is currently active. If it is, the IMS session must be formally terminated to release all IMS database resources before the program ends.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The termination sequence is in progress and the IMS PSB cleanup step has been completed (or skipped)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system checks whether the MQ Request Queue is currently open
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the MQ Request Queue is open, the system must issue a formal close command to release the queue connection and resources; if the close is successful, the queue is marked as closed; if the close fails, a Warning-level MQ error is logged with the error location code 'M005', both the completion code and reason code, and the message 'FAILED TO CLOSE REQUEST MQ' — and processing continues to program end; if the MQ Request Queue was not open, this step is skipped entirely

all_rules.Rule_Name: Close MQ Request Queue on Shutdown
all_rules.Rule_Description: During the termination sequence, the system must check whether the MQ Request Queue is currently open. If it is, the queue must be formally closed to release the message queue connection and resources. If the close operation itself fails, a warning is logged but the program still proceeds to end.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All active resources have been released — IMS PSB session terminated if it was active, and MQ Request Queue closed if it was open — as part of either a critical error termination or normal end-of-processing
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The resource cleanup sequence has completed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program must formally end execution and return control, preventing any further authorization message processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: End Program Execution After Resource Cleanup
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all active resources have been released (IMS PSB terminated and MQ queue closed as applicable), the program must formally end execution and return control, ensuring no further authorization processing occurs.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization decision has been made (either approved or declined) and the response reason code field has not yet been assigned
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to assign the decline reason code for the authorization response
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The authorization response reason code (PA-RL-AUTH-RESP-REASON) must be set to '0000' as the default value before any condition-specific reason code is evaluated or assigned

all_rules.Rule_Name: Initialize Default Decline Reason Code
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before evaluating any specific decline condition, the authorization response reason code is initialized to a default value of '0000', indicating no specific decline reason has been assigned yet. This default applies to all authorization outcomes prior to condition evaluation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization request has been evaluated and the authorization decision is APPROVED (AUTH-RESP-DECLINED flag is NOT set to TRUE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system checks whether to assign a decline reason code
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must skip the entire decline reason code evaluation block and the authorization response reason code (PA-RL-AUTH-RESP-REASON) must remain '0000', indicating no decline reason applies

all_rules.Rule_Name: No Decline Reason Assigned for Approved Authorization
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an authorization request is approved, no decline reason code evaluation is performed. The reason code retains its default value of '0000', signifying that no decline condition was triggered and the transaction was successfully authorized.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization request has been declined (AUTH-RESP-DECLINED is TRUE) and the system is evaluating the specific reason for the decline
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Any one or more of the following conditions is true: the card number was not found in the Card Cross-Reference file (CARD-NFOUND-XREF is TRUE), OR the account record was not found in the Account Master file (NFOUND-ACCT-IN-MSTR is TRUE), OR the customer record was not found in the Customer Master file (NFOUND-CUST-IN-MSTR is TRUE)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The authorization response reason code (PA-RL-AUTH-RESP-REASON) must be set to '3100', indicating that the decline was caused by a missing card, account, or customer record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Decline Reason Code 3100 — Card, Account, or Customer Record Not Found
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an authorization is declined because the card number was not found in the Card Cross-Reference file, or the associated account record was not found in the Account Master file, or the associated customer record was not found in the Customer Master file, the decline reason code is set to '3100'. This reason code covers all identity and record lookup failures.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization request has been declined (AUTH-RESP-DECLINED is TRUE), the card, account, and customer records were all found, and the system is evaluating the specific reason for the decline
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The decline was caused by the transaction amount exceeding the available credit balance (INSUFFICIENT-FUND flag is TRUE), and the Card Not Found, Account Not Found, and Customer Not Found conditions are all FALSE
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The authorization response reason code (PA-RL-AUTH-RESP-REASON) must be set to '4100', indicating that the decline was caused by insufficient available credit on the account

all_rules.Rule_Name: Decline Reason Code 4100 — Insufficient Available Credit
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an authorization is declined specifically because the requested transaction amount exceeds the available credit on the account, the decline reason code is set to '4100'. This reason code is only evaluated when the card, account, and customer records were all found successfully.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization request has been declined (AUTH-RESP-DECLINED is TRUE), and neither the Card/Account/Customer Not Found condition nor the Insufficient Funds condition is the cause of the decline
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The card is identified as not active (CARD-NOT-ACTIVE flag is TRUE)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The authorization response reason code (PA-RL-AUTH-RESP-REASON) must be set to '4200', indicating that the decline was caused by the card not being in an active status

all_rules.Rule_Name: Decline Reason Code 4200 — Card Not Active
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an authorization is declined because the card associated with the transaction is not in an active status, the decline reason code is set to '4200'. This condition is evaluated only after confirming that the decline was not caused by missing records or insufficient funds.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization request has been declined (AUTH-RESP-DECLINED is TRUE), and none of the following conditions caused the decline: Card/Account/Customer Not Found, Insufficient Funds, or Card Not Active
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The account associated with the card is identified as closed (ACCOUNT-CLOSED flag is TRUE)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The authorization response reason code (PA-RL-AUTH-RESP-REASON) must be set to '4300', indicating that the decline was caused by the account being in a closed status

all_rules.Rule_Name: Decline Reason Code 4300 — Account Closed
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an authorization is declined because the account associated with the card has been closed, the decline reason code is set to '4300'. This condition is evaluated only after confirming that the decline was not caused by missing records, insufficient funds, or an inactive card.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization request has been declined (AUTH-RESP-DECLINED is TRUE), and none of the following conditions caused the decline: Card/Account/Customer Not Found, Insufficient Funds, Card Not Active, or Account Closed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The card is identified as having been flagged for fraud (CARD-FRAUD flag is TRUE)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The authorization response reason code (PA-RL-AUTH-RESP-REASON) must be set to '5100', indicating that the decline was caused by a fraud flag on the card

all_rules.Rule_Name: Decline Reason Code 5100 — Card Fraud Detected
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an authorization is declined because the card has been flagged for fraudulent activity, the decline reason code is set to '5100'. This condition is evaluated only after confirming that the decline was not caused by missing records, insufficient funds, an inactive card, or a closed account.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization request has been declined (AUTH-RESP-DECLINED is TRUE), and none of the following conditions caused the decline: Card/Account/Customer Not Found, Insufficient Funds, Card Not Active, Account Closed, or Card Fraud
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The merchant involved in the transaction is identified as having been flagged for fraud (MERCHANT-FRAUD flag is TRUE)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The authorization response reason code (PA-RL-AUTH-RESP-REASON) must be set to '5200', indicating that the decline was caused by a fraud flag on the merchant

all_rules.Rule_Name: Decline Reason Code 5200 — Merchant Fraud Detected
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an authorization is declined because the merchant involved in the transaction has been flagged for fraudulent activity, the decline reason code is set to '5200'. This condition is evaluated only after confirming that the decline was not caused by missing records, insufficient funds, an inactive card, a closed account, or card fraud.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization request has been declined (AUTH-RESP-DECLINED is TRUE), and none of the following specific decline conditions are TRUE: Card/Account/Customer Not Found, Insufficient Funds, Card Not Active, Account Closed, Card Fraud, or Merchant Fraud
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system has exhausted all defined decline reason conditions without finding a match
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The authorization response reason code (PA-RL-AUTH-RESP-REASON) must be set to '9000', indicating that the decline reason is unknown or does not fall into any defined category

all_rules.Rule_Name: Decline Reason Code 9000 — Unknown or Unclassified Decline Reason
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an authorization is declined but none of the specifically defined decline conditions are identified as the cause, the decline reason code is set to '9000'. This acts as a catch-all for any decline scenario that does not match the known and classified decline reasons.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization decision has been made (either approved or declined) and the response message is being prepared
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system begins the decline reason code assignment process
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The authorization response reason code in the response message is set to '0000' as the default value before any decline condition is evaluated

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Default Decline Reason Code to 0000 Before Evaluation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before evaluating any specific decline condition, the authorization response reason code is initialized to '0000', representing no decline reason. This default is overwritten only if the authorization is declined and a specific cause is identified.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization request has been evaluated and the authorization decision is APPROVED (AUTH-RESP-DECLINED flag is not set)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system checks whether the authorization was declined
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The authorization response reason code in the response message remains '0000', indicating the transaction was approved and no decline reason is applicable; no further reason code evaluation is performed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retain Default Reason Code 0000 for Approved Authorizations
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an authorization is approved, no decline reason code is applicable. The reason code remains at its default value of '0000', indicating that the transaction was approved and no decline reason exists.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization request has been evaluated and the authorization decision is DECLINED (AUTH-RESP-DECLINED flag is set)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system checks whether the authorization was declined
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system proceeds to evaluate each possible decline condition in priority order (Card/Account/Customer Not Found → Insufficient Funds → Card Not Active → Account Closed → Card Fraud → Merchant Fraud → Other) to assign the specific decline reason code to the response message

all_rules.Rule_Name: Trigger Decline Reason Code Evaluation for Declined Authorizations
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an authorization has been declined, the system must evaluate the specific cause of the decline and assign the appropriate reason code to the response message. This evaluation is only triggered when the authorization decision is DECLINED.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization has been declined and the system is evaluating the specific decline cause
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The decline cause is that the card number does not exist in the Card Cross-Reference file (CARD-NFOUND-XREF is TRUE), OR the account record does not exist in the Account Master (NFOUND-ACCT-IN-MSTR is TRUE), OR the customer record does not exist in the Customer Master (NFOUND-CUST-IN-MSTR is TRUE)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The authorization response reason code in the response message is set to '3100', indicating that the card, account, or customer record was not found; this is the highest priority decline reason and is evaluated first before all other decline conditions

all_rules.Rule_Name: Assign Reason Code 3100 When Card, Account, or Customer Record Not Found
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an authorization is declined because the card number was not found in the Card Cross-Reference file, or the associated account record was not found in the Account Master, or the associated customer record was not found in the Customer Master, the decline reason code is set to '3100', indicating a record not found condition.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization has been declined, and the card, account, and customer records were all found (reason code 3100 condition was not met)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The decline cause is that the transaction amount exceeded the available credit (INSUFFICIENT-FUND flag is TRUE), meaning the transaction amount was greater than the calculated available credit amount
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The authorization response reason code in the response message is set to '4100', indicating the transaction was declined due to insufficient funds or credit limit being exceeded

all_rules.Rule_Name: Assign Reason Code 4100 When Available Credit is Insufficient
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an authorization is declined because the transaction amount exceeds the available credit balance on the account, the decline reason code is set to '4100', indicating insufficient funds or credit limit exceeded. This condition is evaluated only when the card, account, and customer records were all found.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization has been declined, and neither the record-not-found condition (3100) nor the insufficient funds condition (4100) was the cause of decline
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The decline cause is that the card is not active (CARD-NOT-ACTIVE flag is TRUE)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The authorization response reason code in the response message is set to '4200', indicating the transaction was declined because the card is not in an active status

all_rules.Rule_Name: Assign Reason Code 4200 When Card is Not Active
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an authorization is declined because the card is not in an active status, the decline reason code is set to '4200', indicating the card is not active. This condition is evaluated only when neither the record-not-found nor insufficient funds conditions were the cause of decline.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization has been declined, and none of the prior decline conditions (record not found - 3100, insufficient funds - 4100, card not active - 4200) were the cause of decline
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The decline cause is that the account is closed (ACCOUNT-CLOSED flag is TRUE)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The authorization response reason code in the response message is set to '4300', indicating the transaction was declined because the account is closed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Assign Reason Code 4300 When Account is Closed
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an authorization is declined because the account associated with the card is closed, the decline reason code is set to '4300', indicating the account is closed. This condition is evaluated only when the record-not-found, insufficient funds, and card-not-active conditions were not the cause of decline.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization has been declined, and none of the prior decline conditions (record not found - 3100, insufficient funds - 4100, card not active - 4200, account closed - 4300) were the cause of decline
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The decline cause is that the card has been flagged for fraudulent activity (CARD-FRAUD flag is TRUE)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The authorization response reason code in the response message is set to '5100', indicating the transaction was declined due to card fraud being detected

all_rules.Rule_Name: Assign Reason Code 5100 When Card Fraud is Detected
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an authorization is declined because the card has been flagged for fraud, the decline reason code is set to '5100', indicating card fraud has been detected. This condition is evaluated only when the record-not-found, insufficient funds, card-not-active, and account-closed conditions were not the cause of decline.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization has been declined, and none of the prior decline conditions (record not found - 3100, insufficient funds - 4100, card not active - 4200, account closed - 4300, card fraud - 5100) were the cause of decline
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The decline cause is that the merchant has been flagged for fraudulent activity (MERCHANT-FRAUD flag is TRUE)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The authorization response reason code in the response message is set to '5200', indicating the transaction was declined due to merchant fraud being detected

all_rules.Rule_Name: Assign Reason Code 5200 When Merchant Fraud is Detected
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an authorization is declined because the merchant has been flagged for fraud, the decline reason code is set to '5200', indicating merchant fraud has been detected. This condition is evaluated only when the record-not-found, insufficient funds, card-not-active, account-closed, and card-fraud conditions were not the cause of decline.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An authorization has been declined, and none of the defined decline conditions were matched: card/account/customer not found (3100), insufficient funds (4100), card not active (4200), account closed (4300), card fraud (5100), or merchant fraud (5200)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: All specific decline condition checks have been exhausted without a match (the OTHER condition in the evaluation is reached)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The authorization response reason code in the response message is set to '9000', indicating the transaction was declined for an unclassified or unknown reason

all_rules.Rule_Name: Assign Reason Code 9000 for All Other Unclassified Decline Reasons
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an authorization is declined but the specific cause does not match any of the defined decline conditions (record not found, insufficient funds, card not active, account closed, card fraud, or merchant fraud), the decline reason code is set to '9000', indicating an unclassified or unknown decline reason. This is the catch-all condition of last resort.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The authorization processing program requires access to IMS database segments (Pending Authorization Summary and Authorization Detail records)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program initiates the IMS database access session request using the designated Program Specification Block (PSB) name
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: An IMS database access session is requested, and the resulting session status is captured for evaluation to determine if the session was successfully established or if further action is required

all_rules.Rule_Name: Request New IMS Database Access Session
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the authorization process requires access to IMS database records, a new IMS database access session must be requested before any data retrieval or update operations can proceed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An IMS database access session has been requested for the current authorization processing cycle
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The session request returns a status indicating that the IMS database session is already scheduled or active (PSB already scheduled condition is detected)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system identifies that an existing active session is present and must be terminated before a fresh session can be established, triggering the session reset process

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Already-Active IMS Database Session
all_rules.Rule_Description: After requesting an IMS database access session, the system must detect whether a session was already active from a prior invocation, which would prevent a new session from being established cleanly.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The IMS database session request has detected that a session is already active (PSB already scheduled condition is true)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system proceeds to terminate the currently active IMS database session
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The existing IMS database session is terminated, releasing all held database resources and making the system ready to accept a fresh session request

all_rules.Rule_Name: Terminate Existing Active IMS Database Session
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an IMS database session is found to be already active, the existing session must be explicitly terminated to release database resources and allow a clean new session to be established.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An existing IMS database session has been successfully terminated because it was found to be already active
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system re-requests a new IMS database access session using the designated Program Specification Block (PSB) name
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: A fresh IMS database access session is requested, and the resulting session status is captured to determine whether the new session was successfully established

all_rules.Rule_Name: Re-Request Fresh IMS Database Access Session After Termination
all_rules.Rule_Description: After terminating an already-active IMS database session, a fresh session must be immediately re-requested using the same Program Specification Block to ensure database access is available for the current processing cycle.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An IMS database access session has been requested, either as the initial attempt or as a fresh request following termination of an already-active session
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The session status returned from the IMS session request is evaluated to determine if it indicates a successful establishment (STATUS-OK condition is true)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The IMS database session is marked as successfully scheduled and active, and the system proceeds to perform IMS database read and write operations for the current authorization transaction

all_rules.Rule_Name: Confirm IMS Database Session Successfully Established
all_rules.Rule_Description: After requesting an IMS database access session (either initial or after reset), the system must confirm that the session was successfully established before allowing any database operations to proceed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An IMS database access session has been requested and the session status has been evaluated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The session status does not indicate success (STATUS-OK condition is false), meaning the IMS database session could not be established
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: A critical error is raised with error location code 'I001', the IMS session status return code is recorded as the error detail code, and the error message 'IMS SCHD FAILED' is logged; because the error is classified as critical, all processing is immediately halted and the program terminates after logging

all_rules.Rule_Name: Handle IMS Database Session Setup Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the IMS database access session cannot be established after the scheduling attempt, this is treated as a critical failure that must be logged immediately and processing must be halted, as no database operations can proceed without a valid session.

description:
COPAUA0C is a CICS-based Card Authorization Decision Program that processes credit card authorization requests received from an MQ request queue. It validates the card, account, and customer information against VSAM files and IMS database records, makes an approval or decline decision based on available credit, and sends the authorization response back via an MQ reply queue while persisting the authorization details to an IMS database. This is a main/driver program that runs continuously in a loop, processing up to 500 authorization requests per invocation before terminating.
- **Execution Environment**: Online (CICS) - **Database Access**: VSAM, IMS - **MQ Calls**: Yes - **Module Type**: Main/Driver module
### Key Functionalities: 1: Program Initialization - Retrieve trigger data from CICS to identify the incoming request queue name and set up processing parameters including wait interval for message retrieval 2: Request Queue Open - Open the MQ request queue in shared input mode to enable reading of pending authorization request messages 3: Authorization Request Message Read - Read the next available authorization request message from the MQ request queue, capturing the correlation ID and reply-to queue name for response routing 4: Authorization Request Message Parse - Extract and parse all authorization request fields from the raw message buffer including card number, transaction amount, merchant details, transaction ID, auth date/time, and processing codes 5: Transaction Amount Conversion - Convert the transaction amount from alphanumeric string format to numeric value for arithmetic processing 6: Card Cross-Reference Lookup - Look up the card number in the card cross-reference file to retrieve the associated account ID and customer ID linked to the card 7: Account Record Retrieval - Read the account master record using the account ID obtained from the card cross-reference to retrieve credit limit, current balance, and account status details 8: Customer Record Retrieval - Read the customer master record using the customer ID obtained from the card cross-reference to retrieve customer profile information 9: Pending Authorization Summary Retrieval - Query the IMS database for an existing pending authorization summary segment for the account to get current pending credit balance and authorization counts 10: Available Credit Calculation - Calculate the available credit amount by subtracting the current credit balance from the credit limit, using either the IMS pending authorization summary data or the account master record data depending on availability 11: Authorization Decision - Compare the transaction amount against the available credit to determine whether to approve or decline the authorization request 12: Decline Reason Assignment - Assign a specific decline reason code based on the cause of decline: card not found (3100), insufficient funds (4100), card not active (4200), account closed (4300), card fraud (5100), or merchant fraud (5200) 13: Authorization Response Preparation - Build the authorization response message containing card number, transaction ID, authorization ID code, response code (00=approved, 05=declined), decline reason code, and approved amount 14: Authorization Response Send - Send the authorization decision response back to the requester via MQ reply queue using the saved correlation ID to match the response to the original request 15: Authorization Summary Update - Update the pending authorization summary record in IMS database with new counts and amounts: increment approved count and balance for approvals, or increment declined count and amount for declines; create a new summary record if one does not exist 16: Authorization Detail Record Insert - Insert a new authorization detail record into the IMS database as a child segment under the account summary, capturing all transaction details including merchant information, amounts, response codes, and authorization status (pending or declined) 17: Authorization Timestamp Generation - Generate a timestamp with millisecond precision for the authorization detail record, computing a reverse chronological sort key for date and time fields 18: Message Processing Loop Control - Process authorization requests in a continuous loop until either no more messages are available in the queue or the processing limit of 500 messages per execution is reached 19: Transaction Commit - Issue a syncpoint after each authorization is fully processed to commit all database updates and ensure data consistency 20: IMS PSB Scheduling - Schedule the IMS Program Specification Block (PSB) before each authorization processing cycle to enable IMS database access; terminate and reschedule if already scheduled 21: Program Termination - Terminate the IMS PSB session and close the MQ request queue upon completion of all message processing or upon reaching the processing limit 22: Request Queue Close - Close the MQ request queue connection after all authorization messages have been processed 23: Error Logging - Log error and warning events with timestamp, program name, transaction ID, error location, error codes, and descriptive message to the system error log queue 24: Critical Error Handling - Upon encountering a critical error, terminate all open resources including IMS PSB and MQ connections before ending program execution
